articles.title: Dominic Calvert-Lewin adds goals to become one of Premier League's most complete strikers - The Radar
articles.summary: Leeds striker Dominic Calvert-Lewin, described as "unplayable" by Jamie Carragher, is the focus of The Radar column as he wins an England recall; plus: Brian Brobbey's unmatched hold-up play for Sunderland and Elliot Anderson's Rodri impression for Man City
articles.body:
Welcome to The Radar , a Sky Sports column in which Nick Wright uses a blend of data and opinion to shed light on need-to-know Premier League stories. This week:

🔺Calvert-Lewin's all-round threat 🔺Brobbey the hold-up master 🔺Anderson filling Rodri's shoes 🔺A player to watch this weekend

It took an assist from the goal accreditation appeals panel but Dominic Calvert-Lewin is up to three goals for the season in the Premier League. His revised total puts him behind only Manchester City's Erling Haaland. He is deservedly back in the England squad.

Factor all competitions and it is nine goals in 15 appearances for Calvert-Lewin since April. "He is in outstanding shape and playing with lots of confidence," said Leeds boss Daniel Farke after the striker's starring display in Monday's 4-1 win over Newcastle.

Calvert-Lewin has always had a knack for getting into the right positions. His shot maps, both at Leeds and for his final two seasons at Everton, show a concentration of efforts from the centre of the box. The difference is that he is now converting more of them.

Calvert-Lewin's wastefulness came to define him at Everton. But he has already scored as many Premier League goals for Leeds as he managed in his final four seasons there. "Sometimes a move rejuvenates a player," said Sky Sports pundit Jamie Carragher.

The underlying data illustrates how the gap between his expected goals and actual goals scored has narrowed as he has gradually emerged from his finishing funk. "Maybe sometimes composure has let him down in his career, but not here," added Carragher.

His goals against Newcastle showed the breadth of his attacking threat. First, a characteristic leap and header to dispatch James Justin's cross. Then, a darting run in behind to reach Tarik Muharemovic's first-time pass and finish beyond the goalkeeper.

Farke described him as "one of the standout strikers in the league" after the game. Now that he has rediscovered his cutting edge in front of goal, it is difficult to argue otherwise.

The 29-year-old offers that coveted blend of speed and aerial strength. Monday's game was another reminder of how he can dominate centre-backs from long passes and crosses, while also making runs to stretch opponents and threaten in behind.

His completeness as a No 9 can also be seen in the numbers.

Calvert-Lewin is joint-top with Sunderland defender Dan Ballard for aerials won in the Premier League this season and stands out as the only player near the top of that list who also ranks among the top 10 players in the division for runs in behind.

Tracking data shows he has clocked one of the highest top speeds in the Premier League this season. His off-the-ball intensity is invaluable to Leeds defensively as well as offensively. "It's not just scoring goals," added Farke on Monday. "His work-rate is top."

Calvert-Lewin continues to lead the press for Leeds, shutting down opposition defenders, blocking passing lanes, and helping his side steal possession in dangerous areas. Only six sides have forced more high turnovers than Leeds since the start of last term.

Availability is of course another huge factor in Calvert-Lewin's resurgence. His injury record made his signing a gamble for Leeds, even on a free transfer. But he has so far avoided any recurrence of the issues that plagued him at Everton.

Leeds have managed his minutes where possible. Farke has substituted him in 15 of his 34 Premier League starts. But he played nearly 80 per cent of Premier League minutes last season, his highest ratio since 2020/21, and has played 92 per cent this term.

The consistency of selection has benefitted all parties and Leeds will hope for more of the same when Crystal Palace visit Elland Road, live on Sky Sports on Sunday, with Calvert-Lewin aiming to score for a sixth consecutive Premier League home game.

On current form it would be foolish to bet against him.

From one striker capable of throwing his weight around to another in Brian Brobbey. The Netherlands international, scorer of three goals at the World Cup, is yet to find the net for Sunderland this term but faces Manchester City, live on Sky Sports on Sunday, having served up a masterclass in hold-up play against Arsenal.

His running battle with Ezri Konsa was a sight to behold. Brobbey repeatedly pinned the Arsenal centre-back, showing incredible strength to retain possession from long passes and giving Sunderland an invaluable means of getting up the pitch.

It is an area in which Brobbey is uniquely gifted. According to GeniusIQ , he has recorded more hold-ups, defined as instances of a player using their body to shield a defender from the ball to retain possession, than anyone else this season. He topped the rankings last term too, despite only starting 22 games.

The goals are yet to flow for him but Sunderland boss Regis Le Bris is delighted with his striker. "The game against Arsenal shows that even against the strongest teams in the league or in Europe, he is really competitive," he said this week.

Sunderland will need a repeat performance at the Etihad Stadium.

Elliot Anderson will be one of the players tasked with cutting off the supply line to Brobbey on Sunday. The early evidence suggests the £116m signing from Nottingham Forest is up to the task of filling the void left by Rodri in Manchester City's midfield.

In fact, the 23-year-old, outstanding in last weekend's Manchester derby win at Old Trafford, is making an almost identical number of passes and passes in the final third as Rodri last season, while also winning an almost identical number of duels. The likenesses have so far made for a smooth transition under Enzo Maresca.

Player Radar: Who else to keep an eye on

Could Fulham inflict more misery on Manchester United on Sunday? They are yet to win a Premier League game under Alvaro Arbeloa but in Josh King they have a fantastic young player in fine form.

Five Premier League games will be shown live on Sky Sports this weekend, starting with Brentford vs Chelsea on Friday night.

Nottingham Forest vs Coventry is live on Saturday, before four more games are shown on Sunday, with Bournemouth vs Liverpool , Leeds vs Crystal Palace and Man City vs Sunderland taking place at 2pm before Fulham vs Man Utd at 4.30pm.

Last week's column revealed the numbers behind the on-pitch understanding between Morgan Rogers and Cole Palmer . Bournemouth's Alex Scott also featured, as did Crystal Palace's Anan Khalaili before his goal against Ipswich.

articles.title: In the end, Ole Miss got its revenge on Lane Kiffin in the most satisfying way possible
articles.summary: Kiffin's return to Oxford did not disappoint. The Rebels surged, the Tigers rallied, and then Trinidad Chambliss stole the show and Ole Miss sent its former...
articles.body:
OXFORD, Miss. — On Wednesday night here, in this college town's famous entertainment district, the Square, Ole Miss fans filled the historic Lyric Theater for a special occasion.

Participants threw darts at cardboard cutouts of his effigy, unveiled a less-than-flattering bust of the coach and, from a mic'd podium, ridiculed the man who fled this place in a blaze of ever-loving glory for rival LSU .

Three days later, the football-playing Rebels roasted Lane.

Whose offensive line backpedaled all night in a trench beatdown?

Whose defensive secondary failed to cover receivers in a collapse?

Whose offense didn't score until the final two minutes of the first half?

Whose team fell behind 24-7, stormed back with a third-quarter rally and then lost against the very school he left nine months ago?

Amid a hate-charged, booze-fueled sea of the angriest dang Southern folk you'd ever see, the party who was rejected in this star-crossed relationship, the one left in pieces, the lover abandoned at the altar, the Ole Miss Rebels, they exacted their revenge on the one who got (flew) away.

In the most satisfying roast imaginable, the final joke landed with quite the punchline:

For the Oxford crowd, for those madder'n hell, as they might say here, for those angrier than heck, ticked off, p'ed off and just plain unhappy, this one felt good.

You need only to watch and listen to a rocking Vaught-Hemingway Stadium. As LSU's final play failed — on fourth-and-goal from the 6-yard line – as quarterback Sam Leavitt 's pass whistled into the arms of an Ole Miss defensive back, fireworks exploded overhead, 'Dancing Queen' played over the speakers and beer flung into the air.

The stadium — at max capacity, no inch spared, no seat empty — remained almost completely full for more than a half-hour after the clock hit zeroes. As LSU players left the turf, the stadium operator provided some Louisiana exit music: "Callin' Baton Rouge" and "Neck."

The crowd here released into the muggy Mississippi air nine months of buried anger. Wearing his trademark white visor and long-sleeve shirt, in his khaki slacks and flanked by a half-dozen Louisiana highway patrol officers, Kiffin exited the stage of this dramatic motion picture.

"Get the f*** off our field!" a fan screamed his way.

The man who broke hearts here had his heart broken.

Afterward, he acknowledged it, too. As LSU's team buses arrived at Vaught-Hemingway Stadium two hours before kickoff, Kiffin felt unexpected emotions, he said. Not hate, anger or fear. But gratitude for his six seasons at this place.

As he entered the stadium, he waved to Rebels fans hurling insults his way.

"Sometimes you can't predict your emotions," he said afterward from a small interview room within this venue's bowels. "Sometimes I don't act like it, but I'm human too."

Kiffin lauded an atmosphere that he'd never seen before in Oxford, a stadium full an hour ahead of kickoff, a crowd so loud that his team committed a host of costly pre-snap penalties — none more significant than a false start on second-and-goal on the game's final drive.

Amid an emotional news conference, much of it spent praising the atmosphere and his former underling, Ole Miss coach Pete Golding, Kiffin, long critical of the fickle fans here, couldn't resist the smallest of jabs over their rambunctious behavior Saturday night.

"I guess I had to leave to get them to do that," Kiffin said.

On the field, the Ole Miss team was even louder.

The Rebels won despite missing running back Kewan Lacy for the entire second half . They won despite blowing that 17-point lead (LSU, at one point, scored 17 consecutive points to tie the game). They won despite such a high-pressure affair.

They won, mostly, because of Trinidad Chambliss , who carved through his old coach's defense like a hot switchblade through Mississippi butter: 363 passing yards, 33 completions, three total touchdowns. In what served as the game-winner, he dashed for 14 yards down the LSU sideline, whistling directly by the man who signed him 18 months ago out of the Division II level, who helped turn him into a star, who, as it turns out, assisted in him gaining his additional year of eligibility.

Chambliss makes "Houdini plays," says Kiffin. He's the most difficult player in America to defend, he added. Some of the on-the-run, perfectly accurate, crowd-pleasing plays are inexplicable.

"Best player in college football," the coach said. "I think he gets more dangerous when [Lacy] is out. Now he has the ball on every snap."

He skipped across the turf here, whistled passes to a group of wideouts who made equally impressive catches (nine receivers caught at least one pass).

"The game was on us and we didn't come … it's frustrating," an emotional Whit Weeks , LSU's star linebacker, said afterward. "I wanted to win this one more than any of them. And we didn't."

"This one stings. It felt like a game that got away," Kiffin said.

For instance, on that final drive — a 14-play, 68-yard march that consumed, basically, the last 5 minutes of the game — LSU quarterback Sam Leavitt, all night running for his dear life, missed open receivers at least twice on the team's final four downs from inside the 11-yard line.

In a stat emblematic of the performance, he had more rushing attempts (17) than completed passes (16).

"Their players made plays," Kiffin said.

But perhaps, in December or maybe even January, these two will find one another again — Ole Miss and Lane. Maybe they are destined for a second showdown, a sequel to a blockbuster. The conference championship game or a playoff quarterfinal?

We can all dream. Who wouldn't want to see the second act?

The first top-10 matchup in this storied rivalry since the 1960s delivered a box-office hit. Droves of fans lined up at the stadium gates hours before kickoff, most of them having marched down the hill from the school's famous Grove tailgating spot, sticky and sweaty on this hotter'n hell Mississippi night.

They wore their 'F*** Kiffin' shirts and their 'Go to Hell, LSU' buttons. They drank, they ate. They screamed, they yelled.

And, in the end, they exacted some finality of justice, a retribution never seen in these parts in many moons.

The Ole Miss Rebels roasted Lane Kiffin.

articles.title: El más difícil todavía: dos títulos que no tenía... ¡y en el mismo día!
articles.standfirst: La Intercontinental sub-20 de fútbol y la Supercopa de la Euroliga en básket, nuevas copas en la sala de trofeos del Madrid
articles.summary: La Intercontinental sub-20 de fútbol y la Supercopa de la Euroliga en básket, nuevas copas en la sala de trofeos del Madrid
articles.body: El Real Madrid logró este domingo una jornada redonda tanto en fútbol como en baloncesto, rizando el rizo y con un hito histórico: ganar dos títulos internacionales... ¡y nuevos para sus vitrinas!, que no es fácil por que atesora más de 100 títulos tanto en fútbol como en baloncesto. El primero lo logró por la mañana en un Bernabéu entregado con más de 50.000 aficionados, el título de campeón de la Copa Intercontinental sub-20, es decir, el mejor juvenil del mundo al enfrentarse el campeón de Champions (Youth League) contra el de la Libertadores juvenil, el Santiago Wanderers. El año además ha sido descomunal para los chavales ya que han hecho póker: ha ganado la Copa Intercontinental sub-20, la Youth League, la Liga y la Copa de Campeones. De la importancia del trofeo para el club habla la presencia de Florentino Pérez incluso en el campo para las fotos. Eso por la mañana porque por la tarde, el título nuevo que necesitará nuevo espacio web y nueva vitrina en el estadio, es el de la primera Supercopa de la Euroliga, llegaba con el baloncesto al derrotar al Olympiacos en la revancha de la pasada final de la Copa de Europa. La primera edición de este nuevo trofeo internacional lo gana el Madrid y es el décimo título distinto de la sección de baloncesto. Hasta ayer contaba con 11 Euroligas, 38 Ligas, 29 Copas del Rey, 10 Supercopas de España, 5 Intercontinentales, 4 Recopas, 1 Korak, 1 ULEB y 1 Copa Latina... y desde ahora una Supercopa de la Euroliga. 101 títulos ni más ni menos.

articles.title: Pol Lorente deja la selección mexicana para reunirse con Javier Aguirre en el Valencia
articles.standfirst: La Federación azteca confirma la salida del preparador físico después de dos años en la tri
articles.summary: La Federación azteca confirma la salida del preparador físico después de dos años en la tri
articles.body: La Federación Mexicana de Fútbol ha confirmado el fin de vínculo laboral con el preparador físico español Pol Llorente. Todo apunta a que el español seguirá trabajando con Javier Aguirre en la nueva etapa del mexicano como técnico del Valencia. "La Federación Mexicana de Fútbol informa que Pol Lorente concluye su etapa como preparador físico de la selección nacional de México. Agradecemos su compromiso y dedicación durante los dos años que formó parte de esta institución, desde su incorporación en agosto de 2024", escribió la entidad en un comunicado. Lorente debía ser parte de la comisión técnica del nuevo seleccionador, Rafael Márquez, quien fue presentado esta semana. "Para la fecha FIFA de septiembre y octubre, en la que México enfrentará a Colombia, Perú, Estados Unidos y Chile, la preparación física del equipo estará a cargo de los especialistas que forman parte de la estructura institucional de selecciones nacionales", anunció la federación. Pol Lorente tiene amplia experiencia en equipos de España y formó parte del cuerpo técnico de la selección mexicana desde 2024 junto al entrenador Javier Aguirre, quien condujo al Tri en el pasado Mundial. "La dirección deportiva de la selección, en conjunto con el seleccionador, encabeza la búsqueda del nuevo preparador físico de la selección nacional; el objetivo es incorporar el mejor perfil al grupo de trabajo. El nombramiento se dará a conocer oficialmente una vez concluido el proceso", concluyó.

articles.summary: Valencia CF y Real Sociedad se enfrentan el domingo 20 de septiembre a las 21:00 horas en Mestalla en el partido correspondiente a la jornada 7 de LaLiga EA Sports.
articles.body: El Valencia y la Real Sociedad se enfrentan este domingo a partir de las 21:00 en Mestalla, en el encuentro que cierra la jornada 7 de Liga, previa a un parón internacional que durará tres semanas por partidos internacionales. El historial reciente favorece al Valencia en este enfrentamiento. El conjunto blanquinegro ha ganado dos de sus tres últimos partidos ante la Real Sociedad en LaLiga, con un empate en el otro, igualando en apenas tres encuentros las dos victorias que había conseguido en los doce duelos ligueros anteriores entre ambos equipos. Además, Mestalla se le ha resistido al conjunto donostiarra en los últimos años: solo ha logrado una victoria en sus nueve visitas más recientes en el campeonato, un 0-1 en septiembre de 2023. El encuentro enfrenta, además, dos dinámicas llamativas. El Valencia busca poner fin a una anomalía histórica, después de encadenar tres partidos ligueros como local sin marcar un solo gol, algo nunca antes sucedido en sus tres primeras comparecencias en casa de una misma temporada en Primera División. La Real Sociedad, por su parte, llega tras vencer al Elche en su última salida, pero únicamente ha ganado uno de sus nueve desplazamientos más recientes en LaLiga y no enlaza dos triunfos consecutivos a domicilio desde finales de 2024. En términos históricos, el balance también es favorable a los valencianistas, que han sumado 62 victorias en 150 enfrentamientos ligueros ante los txuri-urdin, uno de los rivales a los que más veces han derrotado en la máxima categoría. El partido entre Valencia CF y Real Sociedad se juega el domingo 20 de septiembre a las 21:00 horas. El partido entre Valencia CF y Real Sociedad de la jornada 7 de LaLiga EA Sports se podrá ver por televisión en directo a través de Movistar LaLiga. También se podrá seguir el partido a través de la narración de Radio MARCA y con los comentarios en directo de MARCA.com. Desde dos horas antes, sigue la previa y los onces. Tras el encuentro, podrás leer la crónica, las declaraciones de los protagonistas y ver el resumen con las mejores jugadas y los goles. El Valencia CF llega al partido contra la Real Sociedad tras ganar contra el Alavés, se encuentra en la posición 18 de LaLiga EA Sports con 4 puntos. El equipo blanquinegro logró su primer triunfo en la última jornada, con el entrenador interino Óscar Sánchez. La Real Sociedad llega al partido contra el Valencia CF tras perder contr el Atlético, se encuentra en la posición 13 de LaLiga EA Sports con 7 puntos. El equipo de Matarazzo llega a este encuentro tras dos derrotas consecutivas, la última, el miércoles ante el Bournemouth en la Europa League.

articles.summary: Simeone podría introducir algún cambio con respecto al choque ante Osasuna
articles.body: Con las bajas de Barrios y Sorloth. Así se presenta el Atlético al derbi ante el Real Madrid. El resto de piezas estarán disponibles y Simeone tiene diferentes alternativas para elegir. El entrenador argentino ocultó sus piezas en el último ensayo en una sesión marcada por el trabajo de recuperación tras varias semanas prácticamente sin descanso. El regreso de Julián Alvarez tras estar ausente ante Real Sociedad y Osasuna, ofrece una nueva alternativa al míster. Una de las principales dudas es saber qué futbolista ocupará el sitio de Pablo Barrios. Desde que el canterano fuese baja en San Sebastián, el Cholo ha formado con dos centros del campo diferentes. En Anoeta la pareja fue la formada por Hjulmand y Llorente, mientras que ante Osasuna la dupla la formaron Koke y Cardoso. El gran partido del norteamericano ante los de Ramis podría darle opciones en un once que parece complicado de adivinar. La polivalencia de Llorente le podría llevar a una medular que será uno de los puntos clave del choque. Su presencia en el medio del campo abriría la opción de ver a Pubill en el lateral diestro. Otra de las grandes dudas será la posición del lateral izquierdo. Con Grimaldo en clara progresión en los últimos duelos, no habría que descartar la posibilidad de que el costado zurdo fuese ocupado por Hancko como en Liverpool. Es cierto que ese día contó con la ayuda de Giuliano en esa banda. Polivalencia y dudas por resolver en el once del Cholo. articles.title: Everyone is glad Lane Kiffin week is over, especially the LSU football coach
articles.summary: Even Lane Kiffin has a limit, it seems. He's happy the massive buildup to LSU's Week 3 game against Ole Miss is over.
articles.body:
OXFORD — LSU football coach Lane Kiffin is glad his return to Ole Miss is finished.

Kiffin has become college football's coaching firebrand because of his ability to attract attention; for reasons good and bad. Leaving Ole Miss for rival LSU days before the Rebels' first College Football Playoff game last year was defining event in a dramatic career.

Since then, he's drawn headlines for attempting to add former NFL training camp cuts Dae'Quan Wright and Zxavian Harris to the roster, which forced the SEC to threaten the expulsion of LSU. A recent book on him is even subtitled "College football's agent of chaos."

Ole Miss football vs LSU, Lane Kiffin returns top photos, Trinidad Chambliss, Kewan Lacy

And yet, in an emotionally exhausting return to Vaught-Hemingway Stadium billed as one of the greatest villain spectacles in recent sports history, Kiffin said he's glad it's over. No. 9 Ole Miss beat his No. 7 Tigers 32-24 on Sept. 19.

"Yeah. I'm sure I'll be criticized for saying that, but yeah, I am," Kiffin said. "I was thinking that all week. Especially today. I would have said that in a win or a loss."

The Rebels jumped ahead 10-0 in the first quarter and led 24-7 at halftime. Kiffin attributed his team's slow start to "walking into a storm" that the Ole Miss crowd created. There were a record 70,033 fans on hand who paid a record amount of money for opportunity to boo Kiffin.

Kiffin said he felt the storm building up throughout the week. It was hard not to.

Ole Miss and Mississippi law enforcement combined to bring in extra police officers to staff the game.

Because of City Ordinance 7.2.5 that bars "pennants, spinners, streamers, balloons and bedsheets" from being attached to the exterior of residential or commercial buildings, the Oxford Police Department had to remove bedsheets with designs making fun of Kiffin.

There was even an official "Roast of Lane Kiffin" on Sept. 16 at a concert venue on The Oxford Square.

Fans at ESPN's "College GameDay" picked up where the comedians left off with signs and chants on Sept. 19 in The Grove. Ole Miss fans plastered images of Kiffin in 2020, before his significant weight loss transformation that he credits hot yoga and sobriety to, on gameday buttons and T-shirts.

The firehose of attention culminated at the game. Profane chants directed toward Kiffin could be heard early and often.

Kiffin said he was surprised by his emotions his return brought on. The six seasons he spent at Ole Miss is the longest tenure in his coaching career.

"There's a lot of stuff," Kiffin said. "Six years here. A lot of life-changing experiences. A lot of really good people that helped me through some really hard times."

Ole Miss fans blame Kiffin for the vitriol. Lifelong fan Jacob Gaines likened his departure in 2025 to "throwing the finger up". Oxford resident Cassidy Jones said The Magnolia Bowl is " more personal now ." Die-hard fan Tucker Johnson said Kiffin is into coaching more for celebrity status than footbal l.

The environment made Kiffin feel more like a normal person than ever.

"I know that sometimes I don't act like it, but I'm a human too," Kiffin said.

articles.title: Buffalo coach Pete Lembo praises Penn State following Week 3 game
articles.summary: Buffalo head coach Pete Lembo believes Penn State will have a good 2026 season.
articles.body:
As if being a head coach of a college football program was not challenging enough, it becomes increasingly more challenging when having to face the media to talk about a blowout loss on the road. Such was the case for Buffalo head coach Pete Lembo in Week 3, when Buffalo came up on the wrong end of a 55-13 drubbing by the Nittany Lions .

As much as Lembo may not want to admit it, the final result was pretty much to be expected given the pregame betting lines. But that doesn't mean Lembo didn't have any reasons to be disappointed in the outcome. Regardless, Lembo offered some praise to Penn State in his postgame comments.

"They play very cohesively, whether they're playing coverage or bringing pressure," Lembo said in his postgame press conference when asked to assess Penn State's performance. "You know, you're looking at some elite players, and they can roll through them too. They roll two or three deep through at each position, and they're able to stay very fresh throughout the course of the game."

Penn State entered the 2026 season with a significantly overhauled roster thanks to a coaching change and the fallout of the transfer portal's impact on the change. New head coach Matt Campbell saw a large number of his former players at Iowa State follow him to State College. Many of those players stepped right into meaningful roles on both sides of the football. Among the players taking on lead roles for the Nittany Lions are quarterback Rocco Becht , tight end Ben Brahmer, and linebacker Kooper Ebel and Caleb Bacon. And Penn State still had some key players opting to stay with the Nittany Lions from last season's roster, such as linebacker Tony Rojas and rising star wide receiver Koby Howard.

"That's a good football team, and I'm sure they're going to have a lot of success this year," Lembo said in his postgame press conference.

Penn State hosts Wisconsin on Saturday, Sept. 26 at 5:00 p.m. ET. The game will air on Peacock.

articles.title: 'I already had a war in summer': Undav's fight against criticism
articles.summary: VfB Stuttgart forward Deniz Undav has vowed to fight back yet again after criticism on his slow start into the season which has resulted in not being nominat...
articles.body:
VfB Stuttgart forward Deniz Undav has vowed to fight back yet again after criticism on his slow start into the season which has resulted in not being nominated by new national team coach Jürgen Klopp.

"I speak openly, I don't mince my words, I say what I think, whether it's negative or positive. And as I said, I've often had problems, I often have to prove myself, as I said," Undav told Sky TV after Stuttgart's 1-0 Bundesliga defeat against leaders Borussia Dortmund .

"I already had a war this summer, and now I have to prove myself again."

Undav is yet to score this season and despite nine goals in 13 Germany caps, including three as a substitute at the World Cup in summer, never had a full breakthrough in the national team.

Then coach Julian Nagelsmann also made a disrespectful remark towards him after scored a late winner in a March friendly against Ghana , for which Nagelsmann later apologised.

Undav has not had the classic football career through a top academy but rather worked his way up from fourth-tier Havelse to Stuttgart, where he has played since 2023 and is their new captain. He earned his first Germany cap at age 27.

"I've had that my whole life, no matter where I was, it didn't work out at first because people say, your body language, you're not a sprinter. But that's how it's been my whole life," he said.

"So I had 39 goals and assists last year and my body language was the same. That's why you first have to get used to it. And when you come into contact with it and know me as a person, then you know how to handle it."

The fitness debate arose again when Klopp didn't pick him into the Nations League squad on Thursday.

But Undav vowed: "Hopefully in November, when I can recommend myself and am back in the squad, the national team coach will know what kind of person I am."

articles.title: Michael Pittman Jr. Fantasy Week 2 Start or Sit: An 8.1% Target Share Is a Sit
articles.summary: Pittman led Pittsburgh in receiving yards in his first contest with the franchise, and he still lands 38th among wide receivers in PFN’s Week 2 rankings ahea...
articles.body:
Pittman led Pittsburgh in receiving yards in his first contest with the franchise, and he still lands 38th among wide receivers in PFN's Week 2 rankings ahead of the trip to New England. Three targets and an 8.1% target share is not a diet anyone can live on, foot injury or not. Without consistent volume, I'm not interested.

Should You Start or Sit Michael Pittman Jr. in Week 2?

Pittman hauled in a 21-yard pass on Pittsburgh's second drive and led the team in receiving yards during his first contest with the franchise.

That's the good. The bad? It's the Steelers under Aaron Rodgers.

Pittman had three targets and led this team in receiving. He added a 28-yard catch later, but in a game with two chunk gains and a 100% catch rate for a player who rarely offers big-play potential, you have to hit double digits in PPR points at a minimum.

The two longer catches were good to see, but I'm more discouraged by the 8.1% target share than I am encouraged by anything else in Pittman's first showing alongside Aaron Rodgers. This game plan was clearly designed around DK Metcalf, and I don't think that was an accident.

Cooper Kupp and Rashid Shaheed turned six targets into just 39 yards against New England last week as secondary options.

There's a world in which Pittman is efficient in this offense, but without consistent volume, I'm not interested (the foot injury doesn't help, though we don't yet have evidence that it's really going to be prohibitive). There isn't a member of this passing game who I'm comfortable with in a neutral matchup, and this isn't even that.

articles.title: Devaughn Vele Fantasy Week 2 Start or Sit: Flex Him Until Tyson’s Back
articles.summary: Vele was the waiver add of the week, available in more than 85% of ESPN leagues entering Week 1, and this 6-foot-5 weapon made the most of a favorable spot....
articles.body:
Vele was the waiver add of the week, available in more than 85% of ESPN leagues entering Week 1, and this 6-foot-5 weapon made the most of a favorable spot. He lands 40th among wide receivers in PFN's Week 2 rankings for the trip to Baltimore. He's a low-end flex in PPR formats for as long as Jordyn Tyson is sidelined.

Should You Start or Sit Devaughn Vele in Week 2?

The Vele production was encouraging, and I fully understand why he was a hot waiver add (available in more than 85% of ESPN leagues entering Week 1). This is a 6-foot-5 weapon in his third pro season and made the most of an opportunity in a favorable spot last week.

I think it continues and he should be in the flex conversation this week, but I also think that this is fuel for the bullish case on Jordyn Tyson long-term as much as it is anything Vele related.

Yes, in theory this adds to the target competition for the rookie, and that's how I think most will view it. It may result in the sentiment trending away from the eighth overall pick.

For me, this was proof of concept when it comes to this offense being able to support multiple pass catchers. The matchup was just right, and Juwan Johnson isn't always going to be taken away at that level, but I'm encouraged.

Vele is a low-end flex in PPR formats for as long as Tyson is sidelined, but I don't mind the idea of cashing in this chip before the end of September should you find a soft spot in your league where a manager is willing to dismiss Tyson altogether.

articles.title: Serie A Preview: Milan vs Lecce – Team News, Lineups & Prediction
articles.summary: After a midweek Europa League fiasco, Milan return to San Siro to take on Serie A minnows Lecce, seeking a way out of the recent crisis. With September’s int...
articles.body:
After a midweek Europa League fiasco, Milan return to San Siro to take on Serie A minnows Lecce , seeking a way out of the recent crisis. With September's international break just around the corner, Ruben Amorim's side must avoid another slip-up to maintain a feel-good factor.

Despite playing three of their four Serie A games this season away from home, Milan head into matchday five as one of just five unbeaten sides (W2, D2). However, after seeing off Torino and Venezia in the opening two rounds, the Rossoneri have dropped four points in their last two league matches.

Juventus scored a last-gasp equalizer to hold Amorim's side to a 1-1 draw in Turin before Diego Moreira 's second-half brace rescued a point for Milan in a 2-2 stalemate at Lazio . Yet, Amorim suffered his first competitive loss in charge of the 19-time Italian champions on Wednesday, as Benfica won 2-0 at this venue.

It was far from a perfect Europa League start for Milan, but they're heavily fancied to return to winning ways against Lecce here. The visitors bounced back from consecutive league defeats with a goal-glutted 3-2 home victory over newly promoted Monza last time out, recording their second win of the season.

Needless to say, this is going to be a much sterner test for Eusebio Di Francesco's charges, not least because Lecce's last Serie A away win over Milan came nearly three decades ago.

Niclas Füllkrug's late winner inspired Milan to a narrow 1-0 triumph in this corresponding fixture last term, keeping their flawless home record against Lecce this century intact. You'd have to go back to October 1997 for Milan's last home league defeat to this opposition, showing just how dominant they've been in this match-up.

Furthermore, Milan haven't lost a competitive meeting with Lecce since April 2006, emerging victorious from their last five Serie A showdowns. As a result, the Rossoneri could make it six wins in a row in this competition for the first time, though it's far from a foregone conclusion, based on their recent performances.

Winless in their last three competitive outings (D2, L1), Milan are at risk of drawing three successive Serie A matches for the first time since September 2018. Returning to San Siro may not necessarily guarantee a route back to winning ways, considering the hosts have lost four of their last six competitive home games (W1, D1).

Milan's recent slump might offer Lecce a glimmer of hope that they could secure a long-awaited win at San Siro, as they seek their first set of back-to-back victories this season. However, consistency has been an issue for Di Francesco's side, with the Giallorossi posting consecutive league triumphs only twice last term.

Despite facing long odds here, Lecce can draw confidence from their impressive road form. They have won three of their last four away league matches (L1), including a 2-0 victory at Venezia on the opening Serie A weekend. With both of Lecce's league wins this season coming to nil, keeping a clean sheet could be vital here.

That could prove a tall order, given that they've conceded multiple goals in 11 of their last 12 league encounters against Milan. Moreover, they've been particularly vulnerable in the opening stages of their Serie A games of late, with seven of their last ten league goals conceded coming within the first 30 minutes.

Amorim has his entire Milan squad fit for this must-win clash. After a stellar second-half display against Lazio, Moreira could make his second Serie A start at the expense of Pervis Estupinan, while Christian Pulisic should line up alongside Alphadjo Cisse behind Goncalo Ramos after regaining match fitness.

Lecce will be without injured center-forward Willem Geubbels , with Nikola Stulic expected to take his place in the starting lineup. Midfielders Medon Berisha and Omri Gandelman are also on the sidelines, meaning Ivan Ilic , who made two assists against Monza, is in line for his second consecutive league start for the Giallorossi.

Milan vs Lecce Potential Starting Lineups

Milan (3-4-2-1): Maignan ; Gila, De Winter , Pavlovic; Chukwueze , Modric , Rabiot , Moreira; Pulisic, Cisse; Ramos.

Lecce (4-3-3): Falcone; Veiga , Siebert, Gabriel, Gallo; Coulibaly, Ilic, Maleh ; Pierotti , Stulic, Monteiro.

Anything other than a win for Milan would be a disaster for Amorim's side, and a bit more urgency from the get-go would come in handy. Each of Milan's seven Serie A goals this season came in the second half, but this feels like a perfect opportunity to buck that trend.

articles.title: Kewan Lacy Injury Update, Diagnosis Revealed by Golding After Ole Miss' Win vs. Lane Kiffin, LSU
articles.summary: An X-ray on the shoulder of Ole Miss running back Kewan Lacy came back negative, coach Pete Golding confirmed after Saturday's 32-24 victory over No. 7 LSU.
articles.body:
An X-ray on the shoulder of Ole Miss running back Kewan Lacy came back negative, coach Pete Golding confirmed after Saturday's 32-24 victory over No. 7 LSU.

Golding said the Rebels' trainers examined Lacy's shoulder and added some extra padding to get him ready to return to the field. The coach opted instead to leave him on the bench.

Lacy ran for 43 yards on nine carries and put Ole Miss up 10-0 in the first quarter with a five-yard touchdown run.

Midway through the third quarter, the junior was tackled and landed hard on his left shoulder. He exited the contest and didn't return.

In general, Golding didn't lean much on the running game. Quarterback Trinidad Chambliss attempted 48 passes, his most in a single game, and threw for 363 yards, two touchdowns and an interception.

The concern for Lacy went beyond Saturday's highly anticipated matchup. He battled a shoulder issue toward the end of the 2025 season and underwent offseason surgery.

Last year, the 5'11" ball-carrier led the FBS in carries (306) and had 1,567 yards and 24 scores on the ground. While Chambliss garnered some Heisman Trophy votes, Lacy's value was obvious to anybody who watched the Rebels' games.

Ole Miss passed a big test on Saturday but still has dates with No. 20 Missouri, No. 1 Texas and No. 2 Georgia ahead. Having Lacy in the backfield will be important for the offense moving forward.

articles.title: LSU's Lane Kiffin Trolls Ole Miss After Making History with New Attendance Record
articles.summary: After coming out on the losing end, LSU coach Lane Kiffin couldn't resist getting in a shot at his old employer.
articles.body:
After coming out on the losing end, LSU coach Lane Kiffin couldn't resist getting in a shot at his old employer.

Ole Miss set an attendance record against the Tigers with 70,033 fans packing Vaught-Hemingway Stadium to see the Rebels win 32-24.

Kiffin thought he deserved some credit for the general energy leading up to the game.

"The stadium was full an hour early," he told reporters . "So, I guess I had to leave to get them to do that. So, you're welcome."

Ole Miss won 10-plus games in four of Kiffin's six seasons on the sideline. Nothing excites a fanbase than winning games, and that's exactly what the coach delivered.

His exit for LSU also guaranteed the atmosphere for Saturday would be electric. The stars aligned so that Kiffin returned to Oxford only months after leaving Ole Miss high and dry ahead of the College Football Playoff.

The anti-Kiffin chants were underway hours before kickoff as ESPN's College GameDay set up its broadcast on the Ole Miss campus.

The fans certainly did their part to make the setting less than hospitable for LSU.

articles.title: Lane Kiffin Says LSU 'Walked Into a Storm' and Caused Slow Start in Upset Loss to Golding, Ole Miss
articles.summary: LSU coach Lane Kiffin chalked his team's slow start Saturday night in part to due the raucous atmosphere inside Vaught-Hemingway Stadium.
articles.body:
LSU coach Lane Kiffin chalked his team's slow start Saturday night in part to due the raucous atmosphere inside Vaught-Hemingway Stadium.

Kiffin said after the game the Tigers "walked into a storm."

"You see it all the time on the bus," he told reporters . "It's how you walk in. It's a buildup. The stadium was full an hour early. So I guess I had to leave to get them to do that."

LSU trailed 24-7 at halftime before coming back to tie the score in the fourth quarter. Ole Miss quarterback Trinidad Chambliss provided the decisive moment with a 14-yard touchdown run to give the home fans the ending they wanted.

The Oxford crowd made an impact early on. LSU was sluggish out of the gate, while Ole Miss scored on four of its first five possessions. Chambliss threw for 248 yards and two touchdowns by halftime.

To their credit, the Tigers were much different once the third quarter started and they shook off a three-and-out on their opening drive.

With the outcome hanging in the balance, quarterback Sam Leavitt guided the offense on a 14-play, 69-yard drive that spanned more than five minutes. LSU couldn't seal the deal as Leavitt's fourth-down pass was deflected behind the line of scrimmage and intercepted by Jaylon Braxton in the end zone.

In a time before the College Football Playoff, especially the expansion to 12 teams, Kiffin would look at Saturday's defeat a little differently. One loss might've been enough to knock his team out of the national championship race.

Instead, the Tigers know they're assured of a CFP berth if they run the table, and they can likely afford to lose another game and still finish in the top 12.

The experience they gained from playing in hostile territory should serve Kiffin's players well for the rest of the season.

articles.title: Mourinho, con el mismo plan de Xabi Alonso un año después
articles.standfirst: El Madrid sale en el Metropolitano con el mismo centro del campo y ataque que hace un año, en la tarde del 5-2
articles.summary: El Madrid sale en el Metropolitano con el mismo centro del campo y ataque que hace un año, en la tarde del 5-2
articles.body: José Mourinho se la juega en el derbi con una apuesta que inevitablemente lleva a mirar justo un año atrás, a la tarde del 5-2. Después de una revolución en verano con seis fichajes, el técnico portugués pone hoy sobre el césped el mismo centro del campo y el mismo ataque con el que Xabi Alonso afrontó el derbi de la pasada temporada. Valverde y Tchouaméni forman la pareja de mediocentros, mientras que por delante aparecen Güler, Bellingham, Vinicius y Mbappé. Los mismos seis futbolistas y prácticamente el mismo dibujo que hace un año. El parecido entre ambos onces va todavía más allá. Ocho de los once titulares elegidos hoy por Mourinho ya estuvieron de inicio en aquel equipo de Xabi Alonso. Además de los seis jugadores de medio campo hacia delante, repiten Courtois bajo palos y Huijsen en el centro de la defensa. Un año después, Mourinho vuelve a apostar casi por los mismos futbolistas. Las novedades están precisamente atrás. Dumfries entra en el lateral derecho en el puesto que ocupó Carvajal (sin equipo ahora mismo), mientras que Konaté aparece en el centro de la defensa en lugar de Militao (lesionado) y Cucurella ocupa el lateral izquierdo en sustitución de Carreras (en el banquillo). El resto, ocho de once, es exactamente el mismo. Mourinho apuesta por los mismos hombres que eligió Xabi hace un año y, sobre todo, por idéntico centro del campo y ataque para buscar esta vez un desenlace muy diferente al de hace un año, la tarde en la que Xabi Alonso empezó a tambalearse en el banquillo del Madrid. Cierto es que hace un año, Bellingham entró en el once sin apenas rodaje tras la operación en el hombro a la que se había sometido en verano. En este encuentro, Mou tiene a todos los jugadores en perfecto estado físico.

articles.title: Lane Kiffin's Surprising Record vs. Top 25 Teams Updated After LSU Loss to Ole Miss in Revenge Game
articles.summary: While LSU's Lane Kiffin is one of the most notable head coaches in college football, Saturday's loss to Ole Miss continued his struggles against ranked opponents.
articles.body:
While LSU's Lane Kiffin is one of the most notable head coaches in college football, Saturday's loss to Ole Miss continued his struggles against ranked opponents.

As insider Brennon Chapman noted, Kiffin is now 13-26 against Top 25 foes in his career after Ole Miss got revenge on its former coach with a 32-24 victory. Percentage-wise that means he is below Illinois' Bret Bielema and tied with Houston Nutt:

Top CFB winners and losers after dramatic slate

Kiffin is far from the only coach who struggles against Top 25 competition.

Coming into the season, Brad Crawford of CBS Sports examined how coaches perform in such games and noted only 10 Power Four coaches in the entire country had a .500 or better career winning percentage against ranked opponents.

That included a handful of national champion coaches, including Georgia's Kirby Smart, Indiana's Curt Cignetti, Ohio State's Ryan Day and Clemson's Dabo Swinney.

Kiffin is still looking for his first national championship as a head coach, and it wouldn't be surprising if he had LSU competing for one in the near future given his ability to recruit top-end talent. He brought in 247Sports' top-ranked transfer class ahead of his first season and will have more time to reshape the roster in his image in the coming years.

But elevating to that level will eventually require more success against Top 25 foes than he has enjoyed during a career that featured previous stops with Tennessee, USC, Florida Atlantic and Ole Miss.

Winning at Ole Miss was always going to be a daunting task. The crowd was raucous well before kickoff as the Rebels welcomed back the head coach who left them for their conference rivals before last season's College Football Playoff.

Kiffin himself told reporters his team "walked into a storm" with how intense the crowd was, which surely helped Ole Miss jump out to a 24-7 halftime lead.

That put LSU in comeback mode for the entirety of the second half, but it drew even at 24 in the fourth quarter behind the play of quarterback Sam Leavitt. Just when it seemed like Kiffin's team had all the momentum, though, Trinidad Chambliss directed a 13-play, 75-yard drive that he capped off with a 14-yard touchdown run with fewer than seven minutes remaining.

Leavitt threw an interception on LSU's ensuing possession, setting off a celebration that will long be remembered at Ole Miss.

Chambliss was brilliant with 363 passing yards and three total touchdowns, which was too much for his former coach to overcome in yet another loss to a ranked opponent.

articles.title: Celtic 0-1 Rangers: Ryan Naderi hands Gers second Old Firm win in space of week to cut Hoops' Premiership lead
articles.summary: Report as Rangers beat Celtic again; Ryan Naderi fired Rangers ahead after Auston Trusty's strike was ruled out; Ivor Pandur denied Colby Donovan an equaliser with a brilliant save; Olwethu Makhanya's second was disallowed for handball; Celtic's Premiership lead cut to two points
articles.body:
Martin O'Neill had insisted Celtic's confidence was not "rock bottom" after their League Cup defeat at Ibrox was followed by a loss to Ferencvaros in the Europa League. But, in front of 60,000 of their own supporters, it certainly took another huge dent.

After Auston Trusty's effort was ruled out for offside, Rangers took the lead. Naderi fired in on the rebound after Viljami Sinisalo denied Min-Su Kim as the cheers turned to jeers at Parkhead.

Kieran Tierney hit the woodwork as the champions looked to respond, with Djedi Gassama then doing the same at the other end.

Celtic's first chance on target did not come until after half-time, but Ivor Pandur produced a huge save to keep Colby Donovan's header out.

Rangers continued to push. Olwethu Makhanya volleyed past Sinisalo but VAR also ruled out his effort, this time for handball.

Celtic had some late chances, but were booed off the pitch on the full-time whistle as Derek McInnes became the first manager since 1991 to win his first two Old Firm games.

53: RANGERS CHANCES! The first one sees Sinasalo palm out James Penrice's low shot into the danger area, then Naderi cannot put the rebound home.

54: CLOSE! The visitors believe they can double their lead here as Kim has a shot towards the bottom corner, which whistles just wide of the post.

"It was men against boys, it was the exact same as last week.

"To come and dominate a Celtic team as much as what they did, it should have been more convincing than what it was.

"Celtic are lucky to get out of here 1-0. You look at the changes that Martin made at the start of the game, the subs that came on made zero impact as well.

"Right now, Celtic are a team that's in big trouble."

Former Celtic manager Neil Lennon on Sky Sports:

"He's [Martin O'Neill] changed formation, he made four changes midweek. He's trying to find a recipe to get some fluidity.

"Rangers were the far superior team, not just in physical attributes and running power, but football.

"They played all the football. Celtic were a lot better than they have been in the first half, without being brilliant.

"But second half, totally disjointed, totally outplayed. Outworked, which is the worst thing you can label at a team. Really disjointed, battered, actually battered.

"All the best players were in a blue shirt today. Celtic have a lot to ponder and a lot to work out.

"They've got an international break, which is probably coming at a good time for them. I know a lot of them may be away playing for their countries but there needs to be a total reset because the last three performances in the space of a week have been very poor."

"Knowing Martin, he'll be greatly concerned. I don't like to disagree with him but it wasn't a close game. There was a massive gulf between the teams.

"I can't actually remember a Celtic team getting such a doing at Celtic Park from a Rangers team, which happened today.

"It looked like Celtic were making it up as they went along. Rangers were better in every department.

"Celtic have got big problems. They were smashed by Rangers and that's a concern."

Celtic boss Martin O'Neill speaking to Sky Sports:

"It was a tough game. I don't think there's very much between the teams. We should have created more. We had a lot of possession. We couldn't make the chances."

Asked whether it's been a bruising week, he added : "Of course. It has been a tough week. The history of the club proves it will fight back from these things.

"We're still two points ahead, so when the players get back from international duty, we'll have a rethink.

"It's concerning. Is it a disaster? I don't think so. We have to rethink and reset. It's a time for self-reflection."

Rangers manager Derek McInnes speaking to Sky Sports:

"Really pleased. We had to deliver a big performance and we did exactly that. We played with a lot of confidence.

articles.title: Uno a uno del Real Madrid contra el Atlético: Vinicius, Mbappé y Mou se caen con todo el equipo
articles.standfirst: Análisis de la actuación de los jugadores y de Mourinho
articles.summary: Análisis de la actuación de los jugadores y de Mourinho
articles.body: Otro partido decepcionante del Madrid de Mourinho. Salió sin ambición ninguna (Tchouaméni fue titular y no Bernardo), tiró a la basura el primer tiempo y luego no mostró ni la más mínima intención de reaccionar cuando fue expulsado Huijsen y se puso 2-0. Un equipo a la deriva que se encontró con un gol al final para poner algo de picante a un partido que jugaron con los brazos caídos y posiblemente para justificarse con las polémicas que dejó el derbi. Sin noticias de Vinicius y Mbappé. PRIMERA PARTE: Gran balón largo a la espalda de Pubill que habilita a Vinicius para una contra que generó peligro. Buena parada abajo en un tiró de Kang In. NOTA PRIMER TIEMPO: 6 SEGUNDA PARTE: Nada puede hacer en los goles. Paradón en un cabezazo del Cuti Romero. Despeja con seguridad un disparo de Baena. NOTA FINAL: 5 DUMFRIES: Trabajando bien su parcela en defensa, por donde apenas se ha asomado el Atlético. Más problemas con el balón, con dificultades para darle salida desde su costado y con ninguna proyección ofensiva. La banda derecha la tiene el Madrid inutilizada con Dumfries sin subir y Güler desaparecido. NOTA PRIMER TIEMPO: 5 SEGUNDA PARTE: Ni en ataque ni en defensa, donde se 'come' el pase de Giuliano en el gol de Jonathan David. NOTA FINAL: 4 PRIMERA PARTE: Sólido y ganando duelos. Bien dando un paso al frente para dejar a Jonathan David en fuera de juego y desactivar la primera gran ocasión del Atlético. Asumiendo la responsabilidad de ir a todos los balones aéreos. NOTA PRIMER TIEMPO: 6 SEGUNDA PARTE: Intentó mantener el tipo tras quedarse el Madrid en inferioridad y con dos goles abajo en un visto y no visto. Salvó bajo palos un remate de Julián. NOTA FINAL: 6 PRIMERA PARTE: Sólido, atento en los despejes y bien en las ayudas a Cucurella. Mejorando la contundencia defensiva. NOTA PRIMER TIEMPO: 6 SEGUNDA PARTE: Error clamoroso y que condena al Madrid. Giuliano le gana la espalda e insiste en el agarrón hasta derribarlo estando ya en el área. Penalti y deja al equipo con 10 nada más empezar el segundo tiempo. NOTA FINAL: 4 PRIMERA PARTE: Kang In y Giuliano están martilleando su lado con insistencia y le están exigiendo mucho. Defendiendo con orden y atención. Resolviendo muy bien todo el trabajo que se le está acumulando. Llegó muy bien a la ayuda para evitar que Kang In aprovechase un rechace en el área. NOTA PRIMER TIEMPO: 6 SEGUNDA PARTE: Estuvo muy exigido todo el partido. El Atlético trabajó su banda muchísimo y acabó encontrando un resquicio en el segundo gol. NOTA FINAL: 5 PRIMERA PARTE: Atento a las ayudas en el triángulo con Cucurella y Vinicius por el costado izquierdo. En ataque nada y tampoco consigue poner orden al juego del Madrid, completamente desconectado del balón y con posesiones cortísimas. Recibe una durísima entrada al tobillo de Kang In. NOTA PRIMER TIEMPO: 5 SEGUNDA PARTE: En la organización del juego pierde todo el potencial que tiene en la banda. Él y Mou van en dirección contraria a su potencia y virtudes. NOTA FINAL: 4 PRIMERA PARTE: Se desenvuelve bien en estas 'batallas' físicas, pero ningún protagonismo con el balón. Perfecto en el repliegue para llegar al despeje en el corazón del área de un centro envenenado de Giuliano. NOTA PRIMER TIEMPO: 5 SEGUNDA PARTE: Sin ninguna presencia en el partido ni protagonismo en el juego. Su posición exige mucho más que presionar e ir a duelos. NOTA FINAL: 4 PRIMERA PARTE: Agresivo en la presión e intentando dar alguna intención al ataque del Madrid. Pide amarilla a Cardoso tras recibir una falta cuando enfilaba el área rojiblanca. Recibió una entrada de roja del Cuti Romero, que le clavó los tacos en la rodilla. NOTA PRIMER TIEMPO: 6 SEGUNDA PARTE: Al menos tiró de orgullo y estuvo implicado en el partido de principio a fin. Intentó rebelarse contra un escenario muy difícil. NOTA FINAL: 6 PRIMERA PARTE: Desaparecido en la batalla física y sin dueño del partido. Saltaron. chispas en su duelo con Baena. Recibe una dura entrada por detrás de Baena que genera la primera tensión del partido. El turco le devuelve la falta a Baena minutos después y el Metropolitano vuelve a agitarse. Baena le vuelve a dar otra tarascada importante por la que el Madrid vuelve a pedir una amarilla que siguió sin ver el rojiblanco. NOTA PRIMER TIEMPO: 4 SEGUNDA PARTE: Sacrificado por Mou tras la expulsión de Huijsen para reconstruir el equipo. Mal día del turco, incómodo y vigilado, con dureza en varias ocasiones. NOTA FINAL: 4 PRIMERA PARTE: Sigue sin estar. Un puñado de fogonazos sin apenas peligro. Buena conducción en un balón directo de Courtois a la espalda de Pubill que acaba en una llegada del Madrid. Se le marcha fuera el remate tras una buena acción individual en el área. Lo vuelve a intentar con un disparo lejano que se le marcha desviado. NOTA PRIMER TIEMPO: 4 SEGUNDA PARTE: Se le acaba el crédito y Mou no tuvo ningún miramiento en quitarlo en el 54' tras encajar el gol de Grimaldo y dar entrada a Diomande. Otro partido muy lejos de su nivel. NOTA FINAL: 4 PRIMERA PARTE: Intrascendente. Muy vigilado. Provoca una amarilla a Pubill, que cortó en falta una arrancada del francés. Se deja caer en el área ante Pubill. NOTA PRIMER TIEMPO: 4 SEGUNDA PARTE: Con el equipo en inferioridad ya pudo hace menos de lo que ya estaba haciendo. Generó más peligro Diomande que él. NOTA FINAL: 4 SEGUNDA PARTE: Sustituye a Vinicius en el 54'. Falla un mano a mano ante Oblak en una jugada que pedía resolverse de otra manera. NOTA FINAL: 5 SEGUNDA PARTE: Sustituye a Güler en el 54'. Marcó el gol que acercó al Madrid en el marcador en un gran remate de cabeza. NOTA FINAL: 6 SEGUNDA PARTE: Sustituye a Tchouaméni en el 54'. Salió con el partido ya muy cuesta arriba. NOTA FINAL: 5 SEGUNDA PARTE: Sustituye a Bellingham en el 80'. Dio la asistencia a Rüdiger en una falta muy bien sacada. NOTA FINAL: 6. PRIMERA PARTE: El equipo no ha tenido el control del partido en ningún momento. Se ha defendido bien y con orden concediendo poco o nada, pero en ataque no ha generado absolutamente nada en un partido que necesita ganar. NOTA PRIMER TIEMPO: 5 SEGUNDA PARTE: Otra actuación decepcionante del equipo. Cero ambición desde el minuto uno cuando necesitaba ganar. Un primer tiempo tirado a la basura con ninguna amenaza y ningún control del partido. Luego llegó la roja de Huijsen y el equipo desapareció. En Liga, dos derrotas, dos partidos ganados 'in extremis' y el Barça ya viéndole a lo lejos en el liderato. Un equipo sin alma, sin juego y sin ambición... NOTA FINAL: 4

articles.title: A este Sabadell no le para nadie
articles.standfirst: Los de Costa ganaron y dominaron al Oviedo y se muestran intratables en la Nova Creu Alta
articles.summary: Los de Costa ganaron y dominaron al Oviedo y se muestran intratables en la Nova Creu Alta
articles.body: El Sabadell sigue soñando despierto y, tras lograr un doble ascenso consecutivo histórico, está firmando un regreso a LaLiga Hypermotion extraordinario. Este domingo celebró el tercer triunfo en tres partidos en la Nova Creu Alta con un merecido 3-1 ante el Oviedo, un equipo que el año pasado competía dos categorías por encima, y podría dormir en puestos de playoffs. Son ocho puntos por encima de la permanencia: era el objetivo a principio de temporadas y va camino de no ser más que el punto de partida si los de Ferran Costa siguen enamorando a propios y a extraños. El Sabadell quería dejar atrás la derrota de Mallorca y desde el inicio sometió al adversario a base de hambre e intensidad. Solo necesitó medio minuto para avisar con una ocasión franca de gol de Ton Ripoll. Julián Calero se desgañitaba en el banquillo. El Sabadell era netamente superior y recogió el premio a su ambición en el minuto 23: Joel Priego puso un centro delicioso en el área y Gastón Valles cabeceó para gritar su primer tanto como arlequinado. El Oviedo intentó reaccionar y José Luis Catalá tuvo que intervenir de forma providencial para evitar el empate de Alexandru Isfan en la única ocasión peligrosa visitante del primer acto. El Sabadell, muy cómodo, seguía oliendo sangre y encarriló el partido en el minuto 44 con el 2-0. Lo firmó Óscar Sanz en un córner servido por Ton Ripoll. Calero introdujo tres cambios en el entretiempo y Estanis Pedrola recortó distancias con un precioso disparo (67'), pero su equipo no mereció el empate y los locales sellaron el triunfo con un tanto de Ángel Baena tras una bella pared con Quadri Liameed. El Sabadell le endosó un 3-1 a un equipo que tan solo había encajado un gol en los cinco partidos anteriores. La Nova Creu Alta sigue soñando.

articles.title: Wolves 1-0 West Brom: Fer Lopez scores winner after Nat Phillips error to seal derby win
articles.summary: Report and free match highlights from the Sky Bet Championship match between Wolverhampton Wanderers and West Bromwich Albion at Molineux on Sunday; Fer Lopez scored the second-half winner in the Black Country derby
articles.body:
Lopez took advantage of a mistake by Nat Phillips after 50 minutes when the Albion defender played the ball straight to the Wolves forward, who scored his fifth goal of the season.

Goalkeeper Max O'Leary had kept West Brom in the game during the first half with three outstanding saves as Wolves dominated, with forward Mateus Mane causing problems for James Morrison's side.

Wolves deserved the victory on a day when Albion rarely threatened in the first Molineux meeting between the West Midlands rivals in 14 years.

The match produced a partisan atmosphere from a 30,000 crowd, but Albion were the ones who failed to react.

Wolves head coach, Cesar Peixoto, in his first season at the club, led the celebrations when the final whistle blew.

O'Leary produced the first of a trio of saves with a spectacular 11th-minute stop to keep out a header from Wolves defender Nasser Djiga.

Kieran Trippier, returning at right-back after recovering from a knee injury, delivered a cross for Marshall Munetsi, whose header was blocked. The ball fell to Djiga, but O'Leary tipped the ball on to the underside of the crossbar.

Mane looked sharp and Jayson Molumby was booked by referee Josh Smith for bringing down the Wolves forward, who then tested O'Leary with an angled drive that the Albion goalkeeper blocked at his near post.

O'Leary then made it a trio of saves with another superb stop.

Mane's cross was met by Munetsi whose close-range header was goalbound. But O'Leary showed excellent reflexes to change direction and keep the ball out with an outstretched hand.

Wolves maintained pressure on the Albion goal and Mane created another opening after 37 minutes, but Lopez sliced his shot wide.

Lopez was alert to the situation when Albion lost concentration after the break while playing out from the back.

O'Leary rolled the ball out and his defence looked in control until Phillips played a pass straight into Lopez's path.

The Spanish forward made the most of the opportunity and clipped a shot over O'Leary and into the far corner of the goal from eight yards out.

They almost made it two after 58 minutes when Mane's cross found Adam Armstrong whose shot was blocked.

Peixoto took off both Mane and Lopez, as his side comfortably saw out the remaining minutes.

But there was a scare for Wolves in stoppage time as captain Toti Gomes collided with goalkeeper Jose Sa as both tried to cut out a cross.

There was confusion with Toti floored by the challenge, but he stayed on as Albion tried to force a late equaliser.

"We knew how important this game was to our supporters and for ourselves.

"The players deserved this win, they showed big soul, big organisation and big quality.

"We created a lot of chances and could have scored more goals.

"I liked the way we played, it left me happy. I'm very enthusiastic for all the games. We didn't let them play as they wanted to."

"He owned up to his mistake, but he's been immense over the last couple of weeks.

"Mistakes happen, now I want to see a reaction. We had loads of time after passing the ball out.

"There was a gap to play forwards and we turned it down. That's what I'm disappointed in.

"We went backwards and did that too many times, maybe we were too anxious. It summed up the game, we didn't have the quality at the top end of the pitch and that's something we're going to have to address.

articles.body:
Última hora del Deportivo - Betis en directo

El sensacional regreso del Deportivo de La Coruña a Primera división, sin conocer la derrota en las cinco primeras jornadas y con dos victorias de prestigio, ante Valencia y Villarreal, recibió el pasado miércoles su primer varapalo. El Sevilla se llevó los tres puntos de Riazor frenando en seco el gran arranque de curso de los gallegos. Esta tarde será el Betis quien visite el recinto coruñés en un partido con solera entre un equipo que en su día peleó con los grandes y otro que llega en un momento de forma envidiable y dispuesto a irse al parón de selecciones en puestos Champions y en el top 3 de la clasificación. Y a un rival complicado, se ha sumado también un inesperado virus...

Hidalgo, preocupado por el proceso vírico que sufren algunos jugadores, tiene varias dudas pendiente de ver cómo evolucionan. La primera está en el centro de la zaga. Giménez, Noubi, Bright y Loureiro pelean por ser la pareja titular. Giménez llega con dos partidos casi completos. En el medio campo podría ser una sorpresa Villares junto a Casadó. Amatucci acabó muy fundido el partido ante un exigente Sevilla. En las bandas, Mella tiene opciones de meterse en el once al igual que Jensen. En punta seguirán Auba y Nsongo.

Tres victorias seguidas en LaLiga ante Real Madrid, Villarreal y el jueves frente al Getafe, junto a la lograda en Lille en el estreno de la Champions, son la mejor carta de presentación del equipo de Pellegrini, que después de sus rotaciones masivas ante los de Bordalás, apunta a recuperar un once más previsible al que deben volver Bartra, Bellerín, Fran García, Marc Roca, Fornals y el Cucho. Pocos equipos de LaLiga tienen un fondo de armario tan potente como este Betis...

El duelo del partido: Yeremay vs Abde OPTA

Yeremay vs Abde . El Dépor necesita el impacto del canario, que todavía no está a su mejor nivel en este comienzo de curso, aunque ya ha repartido su primera asistencia. El marroquí, por su parte, es un jugador diferencial y va hacia arriba. Fue clave en la jugada decisiva del último triunfo del Betis, marcando frente al Getafe. Ambos tienen talento y mucho fútbol que ofrecer en un clásico de LaLiga que no se disputa desde hace más de ocho años.

articles.title: El sistema semiautomático no funcionó en el gol anulado a Dotor
articles.standfirst: El VAR no pudo ser utilizado y se tuvieron que tirar las líneas de la jugada a mano
articles.summary: El VAR no pudo ser utilizado y se tuvieron que tirar las líneas de la jugada a mano
articles.body: Una de las jugadas polémicas de la jornada no ha sido protagonizada por ningún jugador en el Getafe-Málaga, sino el uso del VAR en el gol anulado a Dotor en la primera mitad del encuentro. Una posición que parecía milimétrica... pero que no ha podido ser confirmada con el funcionamiento del sistema semiautomático tras una incidencia. La revisión duró varios minutos y la gente no entendía el por qué. Poco después, LaLiga realizó un pequeño comunicado clarificando la situación, ya que debía ser una jugada que hubiera sido revisada en apenas unos segundos. "Durante el partido entre el Getafe y el Málaga de este domingo, y después de un tanto del conjunto andaluz invalidado por fuera de juego en el tramo final de la primera parte, se ha tenido que proceder a trazar las líneas de manera manual por una disfunción en el sistema SAOT. De ahí que el tiempo de chequeo de la acción se haya prolongado más de la cuenta. El procedimiento de chequeo y validación ha sido correcto y, de manera acertada, se ha procedido a confirmar la cancelación del tanto conseguido por el equipo visitante", explicó LaLiga.

articles.title: El arranque de Liga del Athletic carga a Terzic de tareas para el parón
articles.standfirst: Dos empates consecutivos en San Mamés frente a Elche y Alavés junto a una tacada de 8 puntos sobre 18 posibles en el primer tramo del campeonato obligan a una gran reflexión
articles.summary: Dos empates consecutivos en San Mamés frente a Elche y Alavés junto a una tacada de 8 puntos sobre 18 posibles en el primer tramo del campeonato obligan a una gran reflexión
articles.body: El Athletic abre un largo periodo sin competición hasta que el próximo 10 de octubre sea el primer visitante del curso en Vallecas. Los leones, con cinco jugadores fuera de Lezama por compromisos internacionales, tienen tarea por delante. Llegan a la primera ventana FIFA del curso con 8 puntos sumados sobre 18 posibles cuando en San Mamés se han puesto en juego 12 puntos. En los cuatro partidos disputados ante sus aficionados los leones han sumado un triunfo (Atlético), una derrota (Sevilla) y dos empates (Elche y Alavés). El botín es más pobre de lo esperado, sobre todo porque el Athletic parecía querer volar después de ganar consecutivamente a Celta, de visitante, y Atlético. El primera viaje de Terzic en el Athletic no ha sido tan afortunado como anunciaban aquellos días puesto que después del voraz triunfo ante el Atlético ha habido una clara regresión frente a Elche y Alavés, dos equipos que plantearon numerosos problemas de creación al Athletic y dejaron en duda la eficacia de los rojiblancos. “No hemos dado nuestra mejor versión. A ver si después del parón vienen cosas mejores”, significó Laporte. El central, uno de los tres campeones del mundo de la plantilla, espera que la dinámica cambie porque se han sumado “pocos puntos” en el camino hacia los objetivos del curso. “Los pequeños detalles marcan las diferencias”, añadió. El escaso beneficio a los dos últimos partidos en San Mamés llega en vísperas de que el presidente ofrezca junto al director de fútbol de la entidad una valoración al inicio de temporada. Los números dicen que por mucho que se quiera empeñar el arranque no ha sido bueno. No es que los goles maquillen, pero haber ganado a Elche o Alavés supondría rebasar el 50% de los puntos en juego y ahora se está por debajo. El equipo es consciente de que habrá que apretar y mejorar las sensaciones en este tiempo de preparación en mitad del torneo que ofrece la ventana FIFA para no fallar en un regreso que llevará al Athletic a jugar de seguido como visitante frente a Rayo, Valencia y Levante. Después llegarán dos compromisos ligueros como locales ante Getafe y Real. “Confío en que con la ayuda del míster vamos a dar con la tecla para solucionarlo”, expresó Jauregizar.

articles.title: Jacquet and Alisson impress - player ratings for Bournemouth v Liverpool
articles.summary: How Bournemouth and Liverpool's players rated during their Premier League match.
articles.body:
Alexander Isak scored the winner as Liverpool beat Bournemouth on Andoni Iraola's return to the Vitality Stadium.

Here's how I rated the players, and you can see how you scored them below.

What do BBC Sport's player ratings mean?

Djordje Petrovic: Quiet first half but made a good save with his feet to keep out Bradley Barcola. No chance of stopping Isak's goal. 6

Adam Smith: Good shift on his 431st appearance for Bournemouth . Largely nullified Barcola's threat. 6

Antonio Silva: Settling into life in the Premier League, and this was another impressive display from the Portuguese centre-back. 6

James Hill: Solid on his 50th Premier League appearance and, like Silva, kept Alexander Isak quiet until the Liverpool forward found himself in space to break the deadlock. 6

Adrien Truffert: Good battle with Cody Gakpo but was sloppy in possession and was ultimately beaten by the Dutchman just before Liverpool 's goal. 5

Tyler Adams: A decent display but will look back at Isak's goal and wonder if he should have done better defensively. 5

Alex Scott: Such a tidy player, especially in possession, and can now look forward to joining England on international duty. 6

Rayan: Scored in midweek and was good to watch whenever he had the ball but didn't get on it enough. Great ball to Ryan Christie after Liverpool scored. 6

Ryan Christie: Started in the absence of Justin Kluivert. Got into some good positions but failed to convert. 6

Marcus Tavernier: Threatened going forward and nearly got an assist when he put in a good cross for Evanilson. 6

Evanilson: Caused problems and had a first-half flick saved by Alisson and another effort denied after the break. 6

Subs not used: Di Gregorio, Soler, Gannon-Doak, Diakite, Sanchez.

Alisson: Made a great reaction save to deny Evanilson and was authoritative throughout. Integral to a crucial Liverpool clean sheet. 7

Ronald Araujo: Looks comfortable defensively at right-back and has had a solid start to life at Liverpool , but didn't do much going forward. 6

Jeremy Jacquet: Another composed display. Made a naive challenge early on to foul Evanilson but responded well and made some great tackles. Good in possession too. Can look forward to joining up with France. 8

Virgil van Dijk: Solid again. Ensured Liverpool weren't punished for a poor first half in attack and continues to be one of their most reliable players. 7

Milos Kerkez: One of three Liverpool changes from their goalless draw at Fulham . Struggled initially and was regularly targeted with the crossfield ball over his head but can't fault him for his effort. Battled throughout. 6

Alexis Mac Allister: Did well to find space in midfield to open the game up after a slow start. Has had a positive start to life under Andoni Iraola. 6

Dominik Szoboszlai: Played with a real purpose. Had a free-kick that went just wide in the first half and was booked just after half-time but a typical Szoboszlai performance - bar a goal from outside the box. 6

Cody Gakpo: Started down the right flank and it was his quality that helped make Isak's goal as he charged down the right and put in a dangerous ball that was ultimately converted by Isak. 7

Florian Wirtz: Another day when the German struggled, though he deserves credit for playing a part in the goal. His attempt was blocked by Hill and fell into the path of Isak. Has to do more. 5

Bradley Barcola: Threatened in phases with a deflected shot saved in the first half. It's still early days but Liverpool want more from their marquee summer signing. 6

Alexander Isak: Had such a poor game initially with a wayward effort and cross that ballooned into the stands but, like a true striker, he was in the right place at the right time and made no mistake with his finish. Already scored more Premier League goals than he did last season. 7

Subs not used: Mamardashvili, Gomez, Tsimikas, Frimpong, Ngumoha.
