articles.title: Suntarine Perkins Stares Down Lane Kiffin in New Video as Security Escort LSU HC After Ole Miss Loss
articles.summary: Suntarine Perkins' smile said it all.
articles.body:
The Ole Miss linebacker stood on the field and stared down LSU head coach Lane Kiffin while smiling after the Rebels defeated the Tigers 32-24 in Saturday's highly anticipated showdown. Kiffin was surrounded by security and escorted off the field, and one of the security members even moved the linebacker out of the way so the coach could get through to the locker room (0:22 mark).

For his part, Perkins made it clear how proud he was of his team after the marquee victory:

Saturday's contest was one of the most hyped games of the entire season, as Kiffin coached at Ole Miss last season before leaving for LSU ahead of the College Football Playoff. It was a high-profile exit given the timing of his departure and that he was going to an SEC rival.

The crowd welcomed Kiffin with a chorus of boos and was raucous throughout the contest.

Kiffin even told reporters after the game the Tigers "walked into a storm," which appeared to make a difference as LSU fell behind 24-7 by halftime. The Tigers came all the way back to tie the game at 24 in the fourth and had all the momentum until Trinidad Chambliss put his team on his back.

The Ole Miss quarterback capped off a 13-play, 75-yard drive with a 14-yard touchdown run, and the Rebels defense then picked off Sam Leavitt on LSU's final possession.

Perkins finished with four tackles, one pass defended and a stare down in the aftermath of the game.

It was the stare down that stood out the most.

articles.title: Man City 5-3 Sunderland: How the players rated
articles.summary: How Manchester City and Sunderland players rated in their eventful Premier League match on Sunday.
articles.body:
Manchester City went clear at the top of the Premier League by winning a 5-3 thriller against Sunderland .

Brian Brobbey hit a hat-trick for the visitors but ended up on the losing side, while Erling Haaland ending an unwanted statistic with a late goal.

Here's how I rated the players, and you can see how you scored them below.

What do BBC Sport's player ratings mean?

Gianluigi Donnarumma: Could do little about any of Sunderland 's goals but all over the place when coming out for high balls into the box . 5

Matheus Nunes: Was napping when a ball came over the top, allowing Angulo to sneak in behind and lay a pass off for Brobbey to finish. 5

Ruben Dias: Not the captain's best game. Caught flat-footed for Brobbey's opening goal and beaten to the ball in the middle of the park on another occasion. Did make a remarkable goalline clearance to prevent an own goal. 5

Marc Guehi: Will have an assist alongside his name but an otherwise uncomfortable afternoon for the England international. 5

Josko Gvardiol: Failed to close down Enzo le Fee for Sunderland 's second goal but provided the cross for Erling Haaland's goal. 6

Elliot Anderson: The former Newcastle man was jeered throughout by the travelling Sunderland fans, but made more passes than any other player on the pitch. 6

Enzo Fernandez: Curled in a delightful free-kick for his first City goal and the crafty Argentine saw plenty of the ball in the pockets outside the box. Becoming a fans' favourite with the "Enzo, Enzo" chant. 7

Iliman Ndiaye: Started in place of the suspended Phil Foden and was lively throughout. Unlucky not to get an assist after laying a ball on to Erling Haaland with the goal gaping. 6

Antoine Semenyo: Back in form. Twice thumped home for his first goals of the season and kept the ball alive to poke through a pass for Rayan Cherki's goal. 9

Rayan Cherki: Near his best in this game with some delightful touches. Quick feet and trickery helped create City's opener, and stayed cool to stroke home City's second goal in the first half. 8

Erling Haaland: Sunderland had been the only Premier League team the Norwegian had not scored against. Looked like staying that way when he missed an easy opportunity in the first half but he ended that run with a finish late on. 6

Jeremy Doku (on 74, Ndiaye): Returned from a calf injury for his first league minutes this season. 6

Nico O'Reilly (on 85, Cherki): Should have scored seconds after coming on. 6

Subs not used: Rulli, Kovacic, Ait-Nouri, Bouaddi, Allan, Khusanov, Lewis

Robin Roefs: Will be disappointed for the first goal. Tried to anticipate Fernandez sending in a cross but instead found himself being beaten at his near post. 4

Nordi Mukiele: A tough game up against Semenyo, who scored twice. 5

Kevin Danso: Poor clearance contributed to City winning the ball back high up the pitch for Cherki's goal. 5

Dan Ballard: Part of a backline that conceded three goals in the opening 45 minutes. 5

Dayann Methalie: Booked inside 10 minutes of his Premier League debut and given a difficult game by Ndiaye. 5

Granit Xhaka: The skipper helped his side get back on level terms twice in the game, but ultimately went home with nothing. 6

Noah Sadiki: Eyes opened up when he found space to shoot after darting forward, but blazed his effort high and wide. 6

Thomas Meunier: The former Belgium international could have had a shot for the second goal but instead laid it on a plate for Brobbey to finish. 7

Enzo le Fee: The French passmaster fizzed a lovely ball into the feet of Brobbey for Sunderland 's equaliser and his cleverly disguised pass led to his side's second. 8

Nilson Angulo: Could have made a name for himself but scuffed a golden chance wide in the opening five minutes. Provided the assist for Brobbey's third goal. 6

Brian Brobbey: The hat-trick hero. Three finishes from close range but the Dutchman will be gutted at leaving with the match ball but no points. 10

Malick Fofana (on 60, Angulo) Unable to showcase his talent in the half an hour he was on the field. 6

Wilson Isidor (on 68, Sadiki) Regis le Bris went for it with two up top but the Haitian could not find a goal. 6

Subs not used: Elborg, Talbi, Ridd, O'Nien, Alderete, Ahoka

articles.title: El City esquiva un 'gato negro' y asesta el primer golpe al Arsenal
articles.standfirst: Triunfo 'loco' para asentarse como líderes en solitario ante un Sunderland (5-3) al que ni siquiera le valió el 'hat-trick' de Brobbey para sacar algo positivo del Etihad
articles.summary: Triunfo 'loco' para asentarse como líderes en solitario ante un Sunderland (5-3) al que ni siquiera le valió el 'hat-trick' de Brobbey para sacar algo positivo del Etihad
articles.body: Pocos equipos más incómodos que el Sunderland hay en la Premier a a día de hoy. La semana pasada ya llevaron al límite al Arsenal... y han hecho lo propio en el Etihad ante el Manchester City. Lo tuvieron que sudar. Pero sacaron los tres puntos adelante (5-3) para alargar su invicto y marcharse al parón como líderes en solitario tras el naufragio de los 'gunners' en el AMEX. Maresca, tras las masivas rotaciones introducidas en la 'manita' ante el Norwich en Carabao, debía despejar la duda sobre quién iba a ocupar el puesto de un Foden sancionado por su expulsión en el 'Derby'. Finalmente, optó por meter a un Iliman Ndiaye que revolucionó la segunda parte contra el Manchester United. La presencia de dos extremos puros en el once del Manchester City obligó a Maresca a modificar el rol de sus laterales: Nunes no tenía espacio para coger tanto vuelo por derecha... mientras que Gvadiol disfrutó de mayor libertad para sumarse a Elliot Anderson en la construcción para que Enzo se ubicase unos metros por delante. Debía ajustarse el Manchester City y trató de sacar rédito durante los primeros minutos un Sunderland con las ideas tremendamente claras a la hora de hacerse fuerte sin balón para salir rápido al contragolpe. Enzo, sin embargo, tiró de picardía clavando una falta a los 10'. La botó desde el sector derecho y engañó a un Robin Roefs que se esperaba un centro al área. El primer gol con el City por parte del ex del Chelsea hizo saltar por los aires el plan de unos 'black cats' que, sin embargo, reaccionaron de inmediato: recibió Le Fee entre líneas, 'rajó' por carril central y filtró un pase al área para que Brobbey definiese ante Donnarumma. El punta neerlandés, sensación en el Mundial y que venía de realizar un gran partido ante el Arsenal, estrenó su cuenta particular este curso. Le estaba faltando inspiración al City. Pero, en un error de Danso tratando de salir jugando desde atrás que no se suele estilar en el Sunderland, Cherki definió ante Roefs para volver a poner por delante a los de Maresca antes de llegar a la primera media hora de partido. De nuevo, aunque con suspense, la respuesta del Sunderland fue inmediata. Le Fee volvió a sacar la varita y Brobbey festejó su doblete a placer. No tambaleó el City y, viendo que el Sunderland también estaba concediendo, se lanzaron a por el gol que les volviese a poner por delante antes del descanso. Le encontraron en los pies de Semenyo tras un centro al área de Cherki que Danso y Ballard no acertaron a despejar. Perdonó Haaland el cuarto a placer... aunque el Etihad enmudeció con el 'palmeo' de Donnarumma a Brobbey en el descuento que se acabó topando con el larguero. De una nueva genialidad de Le Fee pudo nacer el empate del Sunderland nada más comenzar la segunda parte. Pero, acto seguido, Mukiele y Danso no acertaron a cortar un envío al espacio de Cherki en dirección a Semenyo. El ghanés definió con contundencia cruzando con la zurda ante Roefs. Pero, por tercera vez en el partido, replicó Brobbey para festejar su 'hat-trick' tras un envío sensacional de Xhaka para Nilson Angulo. El dilema era constante en el cuadro 'skyblue': dormir el partido o lanzarse a por otro gol que volviese a abrir brecha. De esa indecisión no estuvo lejos de sacar rédito el Sunderland cuando todavía restaban más de 20' por delante. Salió en falso Donnarumma y Rúben Dias salvó sobre la línea. En ningún momento transmitieron tener el partido controlado. Pero, a menos de 10', Haaland 'cazó' un envío de Gvardiol para sellar el triunfo. Esquivó un 'gato negro' el City.

articles.title: El Como se estrella y pierde el invicto
articles.standfirst: Caen contra el Frosinone (2-0) y se marchan al parón descolgados de Roma, Inter y Lazio
articles.summary: Caen contra el Frosinone (2-0) y se marchan al parón descolgados de Roma, Inter y Lazio
articles.body: El Como está maravillando en este inicio de temporada. Sin embargo, también tiene días para olvidar... y éste fue uno de ellos. Perdieron su condición de invicto en su visita ante un Frosinone (2-0) que se confirma como la gran revelación en lo que marcha de Serie A y, en consecuencia, no pudieron marcharse al parón igualando a Roma, Inter y Lazio en lo más alto de la tabla. Recuperó Cesc a varios jugadores a los que dio descanso contra el Parma el pasado lunes: Chalobah y Álex Valle volvieron a la línea defensiva; Luis Milla acompañó a un Da Cunha convocado con Francia por Zidane; y Douvikas reemplazó a Kean arriba. La noticia más reseñable, eso sí, fue que Butez sentó a Robert Sánchez... dejando entrever que puede haber alternancia en la portería del Como. El partido arrancó con un intento de despeje de Jacobo Ramón que se marchó rozando la madera mientras Butez hacia la estatua. Más clara todavía, eso sí, fue la cuádruple ocasión del Como a los ocho minutos. Palmisani comenzó su 'show' repeliendo un 'cabezazo' de Douvikas, la zaga bloqueo los remates posteriores de Baturina y Da Cunha y, finalmente, Douvikas se volvió a topar con Palmisani. El ida y vuelta fue constante a lo largo de toda la primera parte. Se vieron, de hecho, más de 30 disparos. El Frosinone, sin embargo, estuvo mucho más acertado. En el 14', Romano Schmidt asistió a un Giacomo Caló que fusiló de primeras a Butez y, tras una nueva intervención de Palmisani a remate en plancha de Nico Paz, el ex del Bremen volvió a habilitar a Kvernadze en el descuento saliendo a la contra. Fábregas buscó soluciones realizando un triple cambio al descanso: entraron Samuele Ricci, Jesús Rodríguez y Moise Kean. El Como, sin embargo, se siguió estrellando una y otra vez con el muro levantado por un Palmisani inspiradísimo. De sus siete paradas a lo largo del partido, cinco llegaron en la segunda parte. El Como estaba completamente volcado... pero no encontró la manera de poder meterle mano para recortar distancias. Se libraron, incluso, de encajar el tercero en la recta final por un 'pisotón' de Raimondo antes de definir ante Butez sobre Jacobo Ramón. No tuvieron su tarde los de Cesc y, a la vuelta de parón, espera la Roma. Frente al Como, precisamente, venía de caer el Parma de un Carlos Cuesta que logró su primera victoria en Serie A este curso contra el Genoa de un Daniele De Rossi (2-1) que sigue sin ganar. David Romero puso en ventaja al Parma en la primera parte; Osmajic recortó distancias a 20' para el final; y Almqvist marcó el gol del triunfo en el 80'.

articles.title: Reusser se regala un oro el día de su 35º cumpleaños: nuevo éxito para Movistar en el Mundial
articles.standfirst: La suiza revalida el título mundial en Montreal tras remontar a Zoe Bäckstedt; Paula Blasi termina 18ª y Mireia Benito, 20º
articles.summary: La suiza revalida el título mundial en Montreal tras remontar a Zoe Bäckstedt; Paula Blasi termina 14ª y Mireia Benito, 19ª
articles.body: Marlen Reusser sigue siendo la dueña del tiempo. La suiza defendió con autoridad su maillot arcoíris en la contrarreloj de los Mundiales de Montreal, donde convirtió un inicio dubitativo en una nueva exhibición de potencia. La corredora de Movistar completó los 39,2 kilómetros en 50:24 y aventajó en 40 segundos a Zoe Bäckstedt, plata, y en 45 a Franziska Koch, bronce. Paula Blasi, 18ª, y Mireia Benito, 20ª, fueron las representantes españolas. Reusser no necesitó dominar desde el primer metro. De hecho, fue Bäckstedt quien abrió la carrera con un ritmo descomunal. La británica marcó el mejor registro en el primer punto intermedio, donde aventajaba en diez segundos a la gran favorita. También continuaba al frente al paso por el kilómetro 22, aunque su renta ya se había reducido a sólo tres segundos. La campeona empezaba a despertar. La suiza había planteado una contrarreloj de menos a más sobre un trazado tan largo como exigente. Fueron 39,2 kilómetros entre las calles de Montreal, el río San Lorenzo y el circuito Gilles Villeneuve, escenario habitual del Gran Premio de Canadá de Fórmula 1. La mayor parte del recorrido invitaba a rodar, pero sus zonas técnicas y los últimos 400 metros al 6% obligaban a guardar algo para el desenlace. Ahí apareció la mejor versión de Reusser. En el tercer control, situado en el kilómetro 29, ya había volteado completamente la carrera: pasó con 14 segundos de ventaja sobre Bäckstedt y 22 respecto a Koch. Para entonces, además, había alcanzado a Demi Vollering, que había salido un minuto y medio antes. Una imagen demoledora que resumió la diferencia entre la campeona y una de las grandes aspirantes, lejos de la lucha por las medallas. Bäckstedt resistió hasta donde pudo y cruzó la meta con un tiempo de 51:04. Durante unos minutos ocupó el sillón caliente, pero Reusser ya volaba hacia otro arcoíris. La suiza detuvo el reloj en 50:24, amplió su margen hasta los 40 segundos y confirmó que, cuando la contrarreloj exige potencia, gestión y resistencia, continúa jugando en otra dimensión. La sorpresa del podio la protagonizó Franziska Koch. La alemana firmó un registro de 51:09 que le permitió conquistar el bronce por cinco segundos frente a Elisa Longo Borghini. La italiana terminó en 51:14, mientras que Cédrine Kerbaol, otra de las ciclistas que había comenzado con fuerza, se quedó fuera de la pelea definitiva. Blasi, la mejor española Paula Blasi fue la mejor representante de la selección española. La catalana mantuvo un rendimiento regular durante toda la prueba, pasó con el noveno tiempo provisional por los controles intermedios y acabó 18ª con 53:29, a 3:05 de Reusser. Un resultado meritorio en la contrarreloj más larga que había disputado el pelotón femenino durante la temporada. Más difícil resultó la jornada para Mireia Benito. La campeona de España, décima en el Mundial anterior, nunca terminó de encontrar el ritmo necesario para acercarse a las diez mejores y concluyó 20ª, aproximadamente a tres minutos y medio de la vencedora. España deberá seguir esperando para ampliar su cosecha en esta especialidad. La única campeona mundial española contra el reloj continúa siendo Joane Somarriba, que conquistó el arcoíris en Hamilton en 2003, también en Canadá. Veintitrés años después, el país volvió a coronar a una reina del tiempo. Esta vez, sin embargo, el himno fue suizo y el arcoíris permaneció sobre los hombros de una Reusser que gobierna el reloj sin discusión.

articles.title: Celtic 0-1 Rangers: Neil Lennon calls for Hoops 'reset' but Martin O'Neill insists latest Old Firm defeat 'no disaster'
articles.summary: Rangers beat Celtic 1-0 to cut the gap at the top of the Scottish Premiership to two points; it was their second Old Firm win inside a week; Martin O'Neill's side have suffered three straight defeats
articles.body:
There was also the Hoops' defeat to Ferencvaros in the Europa League as they limped into the international break just two points clear at the top of the Scottish Premiership, as rampant Rangers showed they are ready to really challenge this season with a 1-0 victory at Parkhead.

It is a break that ex-Hoops boss Neil Lennon believes comes at the right time for the team to "reset". But, while O'Neill agrees with his former midfielder, he told Sky Sports their winless week is not a "disaster".

"It was a tough game. I don't think there's very much between the teams," the 74-year-old said.

"We should have created more. We had a lot of possession.

"It has been a tough week. The history of the club proves it will fight back from these things.

"It's concerning. Is it a disaster? I don't think so. We have to rethink and reset.

'All the best players were in a blue shirt'

"Outworked, which is the worst thing you can label at a team. Battered, actually battered."

Lennon, who had more than his share of Old Firm victories as a Celtic player and manager, did not hold back after watching Rangers run riot at Parkhead.

"Rangers were the far superior team, not just in physical attributes and running power, but football," he added.

"They played all the football. I thought Celtic were a lot better than they have been in the first half, without being brilliant. But second half, totally disjointed, totally outplayed.

"All the best players were in a blue shirt today. Celtic have a lot to ponder and a lot to work out.

"They've got an international break, which is probably coming at a good time for them.

"I know a lot of them may be away playing for their countries, but there needs to be a total reset because the last three performances in the space of a week have been very, very poor.

"Celtic have got big problems. They were smashed by Rangers and that's a concern," added Lennon's former Celtic team-mate Chris Sutton .

"Knowing Martin, he'll be greatly concerned.

"I don't like to disagree with him but it wasn't a close game. There was a massive gulf between the teams.

"I can't actually remember a Celtic team getting such a doing at Celtic Park from a Rangers team, which happened today.

"It looked like Celtic were making it up as they went along.

"Rangers were better in every department."

"It was men against boys, it was the exact same as last week."

Sky Sports' Kris Boyd was glowing in his analysis of his former team Rangers as he highlighted the growing problems for the current champions.

"To come and dominate a Celtic team as much as what they did, it should have been more convincing than what it was," he said.

"Celtic are lucky to get out of here 1-0. You look at the changes that Martin made at the start of the game, the subs that came on made zero impact as well.

"Right now, Celtic are a team that's in big trouble."

articles.title: La familia de la portería del Barça crece con Livakovic
articles.standfirst: Excelente ambiente en la meta pese a la competencia: Szczesny ayudó al croata en su debut
articles.summary: Excelente ambiente en la meta pese a la competencia: Szczesny ayudó al croata en su debut
articles.body: El Barça es una familia. Jugadores, técnicos y Directiva no dejan de asegurarlo y de incidir en esta comunión como una de las claves de su éxito y de que atraviese el mejor arranque de su historia. Es un grupo unido a pesar de la competencia que hay en todas las líneas, también en un puesto tan disputado como el de la portería. Lo comprobó Dominik Livakovic en su debut en el Sánchez Pizjuán. El equipo culé está haciendo historia con unos registros majestuosos: ha ganado los ocho encuentros disputados y es una apisonadora goleadora: entre los siete encuentros de LaLiga y el de la Champions League ha marcado ¡36! tantos y ha encajado 8. Y este excelente rendimiento se debe al talento y la calidad de sus jugadores, pero también al buen ambiente de su vestuario, que hace que pese a la competencia reine la solidaridad y el compañerismo. El último en comprobarlo fue Dominik Livakovic. Ante las molestias en la rodilla derecha de Joan García, Flick debía elegir entre Szczesny y el croata, de 31 años, para el encuentro en el Sánchez Pizjuán. Todo apuntaba a que el escogido sería el arquero polaco, confió en él cuando tuvo que relevar al catalán contra el Racing, pero el preparador se dejó llevar por sus sensaciones, según él mismo reconoció, y alineó frente al Sevilla al fichaje de este verano. Lejos de ofenderse, Szczesny fue un gran apoyó y ayudó al internacional croata. "Es muy fácil adaptarse aquí. El entrenador de porteros, Joan, Tek... son chicos fantásticos. Tek ha hablado mucho hoy conmigo, también el entrenador. Me han hecho el trabajo fácil", comentó Livakovic, "muy contento y orgulloso" con su debut como azulgrana. La buena relación de Szczesny y Joan García ya era evidente y notoria, pero ahora también hay cordialidad con Livakovic, como el internacional croata reconoce. Pero esa unión del vestuario va más allá de la portería. El compañerismo es una de las señas de identidad del Barça de Flick: "Desde el primer día, he tenido cerca a Dani Olmo. Jugué con él en el Dinamo de Zagreb hace seis o siete años. Adaptarme al Barça ha sido fácil porque son chicos jóvenes, y es como una familia". A priori, Joan García volverá a la meta tras el parón. Sólo sufre unas leves molestias en la rodilla derecha, pero juegue quien juegue bajo palos, todos van a una. Eso no resta, no obstante, que todos quieran jugar. Pero la competencia es sana y transparente, y eso mantiene al Barça en lo más alto.

articles.title: Norwich 3-4 Bolton: Trotters prevail in seven-goal Championship thriller at Carrow Road
articles.summary: Report and free match highlights from the Sky Bet Championship match between Norwich City and Bolton Wanderers at Carrow Road; Atsuki Ito scored the winner off the bench in a thrilling encounter
articles.body:
The Canaries, who lost by the same scoreline at Middlesbrough last Saturday, again traded goals with their opponents at a rapid rate before Trotters substitute Atsuki Ito had the final say midway through the second period.

A breathless first half saw Norwich pegged back twice after taking the lead through their first attack of the game in the fifth minute.

Andre Brooks slipped in Mo Toure through the inside-right channel and the in-form Australian striker fired home in spectacular fashion from just outside the area, his first-time effort flying past Gavin Bazunu before the goalkeeper had had a chance to react.

Bolton were level within three minutes, however, through another well-taken goal, Thierry Gale cutting inside from the left before beating Vladan Kovacevic at his near post with a precise finish.

Toure then had another effort ruled out by a clear-cut offside decision before his afternoon was cut short after just a quarter of an hour when he injured his arm after falling awkwardly.

Norwich regained their lead in the 19th minute as a deep corner from Oscar Schwartau was headed home off the upright by centre-half Ruairi McConville for his first goal in Norwich colours.

The Trotters continued to look a threat going forward, with a couple of decent chances going begging before they levelled again in the 42nd minute.

After the Canaries had made a hash of playing out from the back, Max Conway was able to play in a low cross that eventually fell for Gaizka Larrazabal, who unleashed a perfectly-struck half-volley which flew into the net from some 20 yards out.

Bolton stunned the home faithful by going ahead for the first time less than two minutes after the interval. A neat attack down the right ended with Kyliane Dong playing in Sam Dalby who produced a neat chipped finish to beat Kovacevic.

There was no letting up with the entertainment, with Norwich getting back on level terms in the 61st minute. Substitute Paris Maghoma made an immediate impact by sweeping the ball wide to the fast-breaking Jack Stacey, who burst into the area before firing home off the far post.

Kovacevic made a good reaction stop to prevent Larrazabal from quickly restoring Bolton's lead but they did not have to wait long for their fourth of the afternoon.

With 72 minutes on the clock, substitute Ito, who had only just been introduced, wriggled his way through the centre of the home defence before calmly finding the bottom corner.

"There were some good moments for us out there today but obviously everything is overshadowed by conceding four goals.

"It was a frantic game - and you don't win many games of football if you concede four.

"I thought we started well and scored a good goal but then we conceded a goal that was too easy. Their winger was surrounded by four of our players but still managed to get his shot away and hit the net.

"Their second equaliser was a result of an attacking player only thinking about attacking, not defending, and then we fall apart as a team.

"There were some hard lessons to be learned but I believe what these guys can do together and we need to reset and make sure these sort of things don't happen again."

"Every game is going to be difficult for us at this level because of what we are up against and this is an especially tough place to come.

"It was a great game for the neutral, as I thought it would be, with lots of chances created and obviously we are delighted to come away with the three points.

"I was really impressed with the character we showed to get back in the game after twice going behind - and then didn't let it affect us when they got it back to 3-3.

"We got in front again and then had the energy and resilience to see out the game.

"We have played well in our other away games this season without getting a reward so I am glad we have finally got something for our efforts.

"I am especially pleased for our fans. Nearly 1,000 came down for a Sunday lunchtime kick-off and gave us terrific support and it's obviously nice for them too."

articles.title: Funes: "Cuando ganemos el primero todo va a cambiar"
articles.standfirst: El técnico sigue intentando arrancar a su equipo
articles.summary: El técnico sigue intentando arrancar a su equipo
articles.body: El Málaga CF se marchó del Coliseum con una derrota dolorosa. El conjunto blanquiazul compitió durante buena parte del encuentro, especialmente en una primera mitad en la que dispuso de ocasiones y llegó a marcar por medio de Carlos Dotor, aunque el tanto fue anulado tras la intervención del sistema semiautomático. El Getafe mejoró tras el descanso y encontró el premio a cinco minutos del final, cuando Iván Azón batió a Alfonso Herrero. Funes valoró el encuentro tras el pitido final y destacó la capacidad de su equipo para competir en Primera División. «Ha sido una pena. Hicimos méritos para hacer goles y no llegó ninguno. Intentamos ir a por la victoria y obtuvimos la derrota», explicó el técnico malaguista, que confía en que el parón sirva para analizar lo ocurrido y corregir errores. «Nos van a venir bien estas tres semanas para analizar todo y resarcirnos de las heridas. Estoy convencido de que la victoria va a llegar. Cuando llegue la primera, llegarán las demás». El entrenador reconoció el golpe que supone la derrota, aunque evitó quedarse en el resultado. «Es un golpe duro. Todos tenemos una ilusión tremenda. Si miramos atrás vamos a arreglar poco. Hay que pensar en mejorar. Tenemos un margen de mejora muy grande», señaló. Para Funes, el equipo necesita elevar su nivel competitivo para empezar a transformar sus actuaciones en puntos: «Lo más importante es ser capaces de competir mucho mejor; eso nos dará la oportunidad de sumar más puntos». Funes se mostró satisfecho con la imagen ofrecida por sus jugadores en la primera mitad. «La primera parte me ha encantado; han mostrado una personalidad terrible y con mucho aplomo», destacó. El técnico considera que el Málaga está demostrando que puede plantar cara en la máxima categoría: «Hoy los nuestros se han visto bien compitiendo. Se han llevado poco premio». Tras el descanso, el entrenador buscó dar un paso adelante con la entrada de una segunda referencia ofensiva. «Hemos intentado dar un paso adelante en la segunda parte con la doble punta», explicó. Sin embargo, admitió que el cambio también pudo generar cierto desequilibrio: «Queríamos ir a por el partido y no conformarnos; igual ahí nos debilitamos por dentro metiendo la doble punta». Una de las claves señaladas por Funes fue la necesidad de mejorar en los metros finales. El Málaga está generando situaciones, pero necesita convertirlas en ocasiones más peligrosas y goles. «Cogerle el pulso a la categoría para tener esa determinación. El partido del Villarreal y del Real Madrid nos costó competir, pero ha habido encuentros donde hemos competido bien. Tenemos que mejorar la determinación y tener más certeza arriba. Las situaciones de último tercio las tenemos, pero tenemos que hacer más daño», apuntó. El entrenador considera que ese paso puede cambiar la dinámica del equipo. «Hay cosas que el equipo hace bien, pero hay que hacer más daño en el último tercio. Nos dará la oportunidad de ponernos por delante en los partidos». Y añadió: «En la primera mitad hemos hecho méritos para hacer gol, pero no tuvimos premio». La titularidad de Eneko Jauregi fue otro de los asuntos abordados por el entrenador. Funes explicó que Adrián Niño todavía no estaba en condiciones de acumular demasiados minutos y que Chupete llegaba muy cargado tras el partido del jueves. «Niño venía de lesión y acumular muchos minutos era complejo. Chupete terminó muy cansado el jueves», explicó. Sobre Jauregi, destacó su actuación durante los primeros 45 minutos: «Ha hecho una muy buena primera mitad, sujetaba a los centrales y recogió muchas segundas acciones». El delantero, sin embargo, vio una tarjeta amarilla y terminó siendo sustituido. «Tenía amarilla y tuvimos que exponer a los otros dos», señaló Funes. El técnico malaguista también analizó la jugada que terminó decidiendo el partido. A su juicio, el Málaga perdió el orden en su intento de buscar la victoria. «Nos precipitamos en el saque, el querer ganar… Hay que tener tranquilidad para ir a por el balón y tener más orden», explicó. Funes fue claro sobre las consecuencias de esa situación: «Una vez que defiendes en inferioridad numérica, te expones a que pasen cosas». Por último, el entrenador fue preguntado por la disfunción del sistema semiautomático de fuera de juego en el gol anulado a Carlos Dotor. Funes reconoció que no recibió una explicación clara durante el partido. «No lo he entendido bien. No sabían decirnos qué pasaba. Ellos son los que deciden, me imagino que la tecnología habrá funcionado bien», concluyó.

articles.title: Nacho Ferri entra en ebullición con el Feyenoord
articles.standfirst: El punta español volvió a 'mojar' en la 'manita' contra el Utrecht (5-0) · El PVS cae y el AZ asalta el liderato de la Eredivisie
articles.summary: El punta español volvió a 'mojar' en la 'manita' contra el Utrecht (5-0) · El PVS cae y el AZ asalta el liderato de la Eredivisie
articles.body: Nacho Ferri, sin esperarlo, se encontró a última hora con la misión de suplir la baja de Ayase Ueda... y está empezando a entrar en ebullición con el Feyenoord. Venía de marcar un 'hat-trick' contra el PEC Zwolle... y volvió a 'mojar' en la 'manita' contra el Utrecht (5-0). El Feyenoord saltó a De Kuip como un auténtico vendaval: a los seis minutos, ya mandaba gracias al tanto de Hadj Moussa y, antes de llegar al 10', Mika Mármol habilitó desde línea de fondo a Nacho Ferri para el 2-0. El punta español dio un paso atrás para quedarse solo y cargó la pierna con violencia. Los problemas se sucedían en un Utrecht que, nada más perder a un Stepanov que enlazaba cinco jornadas consecutivas viendo portería, vio como Hadj Moussa celebró su doblete particular para poner el 3-0. Entraron Cathline, Broholm y Duijn al descanso. En el 53', sin embargo, Valente puso el cuarto de penalti y, pasada la hora de encuentro, Gaoussaou Diarra cerró la 'manita' a pase de un Zechiël -la temporada pasada estuvo en el Utrecht- convocado por Xavi con Países Bajos. El PSV ya parecía haber cogido velocidad de crucero en busca de su cuarto título de Liga consecutivo. Sin embargo, tras lograr darle la vuelta al tanto inicial de Taha gracias al doblete de Guus Til, el Twente (3-2) remontó el partido en la recta final gracias a los goles de Weghorst y Weidmann. Los de Peter Bosz, de este modo, cedieron el liderato de la Eredivisie en favor de un AZ -les derrotó en la Supercopa de Países Bajos- que se impuso por la mínima al Telstar (1-0). Meerdink, en la primera parte, batió a un Ronald Koeman Jr. que, aun así, mantuvo con vida a los suyos hasta el final realizando siete paradas. También le anularon un Kees Smit.

articles.body: El Málaga CF encadenó una nueva derrota en LaLiga tras caer por la mínima ante el Getafe en el Coliseum. El conjunto blanquiazul tuvo sus mejores minutos durante la primera mitad, en la que incluso llegó a marcar por medio de Carlos Dotor, aunque el tanto fue anulado. Tras el descanso, el equipo perdió presencia y terminó encajando el tanto de Iván Azón a cinco minutos del final. Ramón compareció ante los medios como capitán del Málaga y asumió la necesidad de corregir errores en este inicio de temporada. «Es Primera División. Aquí el mínimo error te penaliza y, obviamente, hay cosas que tenemos que mejorar. Hay una gran diferencia entre Primera y Segunda», señaló el centrocampista. El malaguista reconoció que el arranque está siendo complicado y apuntó al trabajo como vía para corregir los problemas. «Nos está costando en este comienzo, pero nosotros vamos a luchar, vamos a trabajar, nos vamos a mirar al espejo las cosas que estemos haciendo mal», explicó. Ramón admitió que el vestuario terminó afectado por la derrota, aunque pidió pasar página rápidamente. «Ahora mismo, jodidos, pero bueno, nos tiene que durar 24 horas, tanto lo bueno como lo malo», señaló. El capitán aseguró que el grupo está preparado para afrontar el parón y utilizar estas dos semanas para analizar los errores cometidos. «Vamos a tener dos semanas en las que vamos a poder analizar todos los partidos, las cosas que tenemos que mejorar. Nosotros estamos convencidos totalmente de que lo vamos a hacer», afirmó. Uno de los aspectos que debe corregir el equipo está relacionado con su producción ofensiva. Ramón no quiso señalar únicamente a los delanteros y apuntó a una responsabilidad colectiva «En tres cuartos es cierto que nos faltan cosas, pero no solo en tres cuartos, ni es cosa de los delanteros, esto es una cosa colectiva», explicó. «Desde atrás tenemos que hacer que llegue el balón en condiciones ahí arriba. El equipo tiene que dar un paso adelante en ese sentido».

articles.title: Bournemouth 0-1 Liverpool: Alexander Isak scores winner as Andoni Iraola triumphs at his former club
articles.summary: Report and free match highlights as Liverpool beat Bournemouth 1-0 in Premier League as Andoni Iraola seals victory over his former club; Alexander Isak scored winning goal after excellent play down the right from Cody Gakpo; Liverpool go into the international break in the top six
articles.body:
A tense game was settled just after the hour mark as Isak latched onto Cody Gakpo's cross - via a slight nick off Florian Wirtz.

Liverpool snatched victory on a day where they struggled in large parts, with Sky Sports' Jamie Carragher criticising their first-half display, as the Cherries dominated. "Iraola probably cannot believe how lethargic Liverpool look," he said on co-commentary duty.

Latest news and rumours: Bournemouth | Liverpool

But Bournemouth lacked the clinical touch as they remain winless under Marco Rose in the league. Their best chance fell to Evanilson, whose near-post flick from Marcus Tavernier's cross was kept out brilliantly by Alisson - who palmed out the effort from behind him.

The victory is Liverpool's second in the league this season as they go into the international break in sixth place. Bournemouth, meanwhile, sit level on points with Coventry in 17th place.

18: HUGE SAVE! Tavernier's cross from the right is flicked towards the near post by Evanilson but Alisson makes a huge stop.

34: SAVE! Bradley Barcola cuts inside from the left wing and his effort is saved by Djordje Petrovic.

36: JUST WIDE! Dominik Szoboszlai hits a trademark free-kick which bounces just the wrong side of the post.

61: GOAL! Isak crashes Liverpool in front after Gakpo did well down the right wing.

68: SAVE! Bournemouth look for a response but Evanilson can only curl into Alisson's clutches.

70: BIG BLOCK! Gakpo pokes Isak through on goal but James Hill comes across for a big block.

90+2: BIG CHANCE! Lewis Koumas has the chance to seal it for Liverpool but his curling effort inside the box from Victor Munoz's pass is straight at Petrovic.

Iraola unhappy with how Liverpool started game

Liverpool head coach Andoni Iraola to Sky Sports:

"I'm obviously happy with the result. I know it's a difficult place to come, very difficult place to get three points. We could see in the game, at the beginning in the first 20 minutes, we weren't at the level at the game, and it has cost us until afterwards, where we finished the first half better.

"The second half we played better. But that beginning of the game kind of - not surprised us because we knew where we were coming to - but it was difficult for us.

"We could see a bit later when Bournemouth started to get tired that in the second half we controlled the game much better. We even had chances to finish but didn't score the second one.

"But that first part of the game, we were not winning duels, second balls and when they play with this intensity, you have to be at their level."

Analysis: Where would Liverpool be without Cody Gakpo?

In every single Liverpool game he's started this season, Cody Gakpo has produced a golden moment in front of goal.

A goal at Newcastle on the opening weekend, a silky against Nottingham Forest, assists for both goals in the win over Ipswich, another assist and a goal against Tottenham in the Carabao Cup - but this intervention at Bournemouth was the best of the lot.

With Liverpool struggling for attacking influence, Gakpo's hard-fought run and cross down the right wing was vital in the build-up to Alexader Isak's winner. "The difficult part of the goal is from him," said Iraola about Gakpo, who is unfortunate not to be accredited with the assist.

But Gakpo also starred defensively at Bournemouth, winning more duels than any other player on the pitch. He shut down one of the Cherries' biggest threats. "I know Adrien Truffert very well and he demands a lot from you defensively. Cody today has been very important in both ways."

Looking at this form, it is absolutely staggering that Liverpool considered sanctioning the sale of Gakpo this summer. Where would they be without him?

Rose: Bournemouth panicked in tight situations

Bournemouth head coach Marco Rose to Sky Sports:

"We couldn't see that one team deserved to win. We played really good in the first 25 minutes and then it got more open.

"We had to work really hard to get chances but we conceded an easy goal.

"In both boxes, you had to be ready and be present. In the end, they scored the goal with one situation and we put a lot of effort into creating chances.

"We panicked a little bit in tight situations. We were fit and I thought we could bring more energy into the game. It is disappointing.

"It was an opportunity to win, right now we have three points from five games and it is disappointing, I think we missed details."

articles.title: Bill Belichick called it, but UNC football couldn't do it in loss at Clemson
articles.summary: It was something that was on display often in UNC's loss to Clemson last season. Bill Belichick's Tar Heels struggled again with this problem in Death Valley...
articles.body:
CLEMSON, S.C. — Bill Belichick called it earlier in the week before UNC football made its way down to Death Valley for the ACC opener against Clemson .

"The big thing with Clemson is going to be tackling," Belichick said during his preview of the Tigers, adding that "tackling will be really important for us."

Missed tackles in a flat second-half showing contributed to the Tar Heels' 28-20 loss against the Tigers , who rallied from an early two-touchdown deficit to prevent UNC from celebrating at Memorial Stadium for the first time since 2001.

"Obviously, disappointing end. Proud of the way our players competed and Clemson's a good football team. In the end, they made a few more plays than we did," Belichick said.

"In the last eight minutes of the game, we missed a couple opportunities on offense, missed tackles on defense. … Disappointing end. Just gotta keep working and getting better, which we are. Really not too much to say."

The Tar Heels (2-1, 0-1 ACC) controlled the game in a first half that included a butt fumble and boos from Clemson fans, but the Tigers (2-1, 1-0) got going just before halftime with an 88-yard drive that sparked the shift.

The energy was even more noticeable after a 2 ½-hour weather delay.

"I don't think we had enough energy. … We just came out kind of flat," McDonald said of the restart.

Clemson racked up 284 yards and three TDs in the second half, including two scores in the final 4 ½ minutes to complete the rally.

"We just didn't play with great fundamentals the rest of the game," McDonald said. "We just need to finish tackles."

Six of Clemson's seven explosive plays — defined as runs of at least 10 yards or passes of a least 20 yards — came in the second half, including two during the decisive final minutes following the delay.

UNC allowed 115 yards after the catch and missed a season-high 15 tackles. Five players were charged with multiple missed tackles. According to Pro Football Focus, the Tar Heels received a tackling grade of 50.4, its lowest mark of the season and its worst since producing a 32.2 grade in last year's lopsided loss to Clemson in Chapel hill.

McDonald pointed to a "lack of fundamentals" and "just us not finishing it" at crucial points in Death Valley.

"We have good play calls, we have good players," he said. "We just have to execute."

The performance marked a sharp contrast from the Tar Heels' first two games, during which they allowed 13 points and held opponents scoreless for a stretch that reached nine consecutive quarters before the collapse at Clemson.

Now, it's back to the drawing board for a defense that wasn't at its best against a vulnerable offense led by a freshman quarterback.

"Obviously, we're disappointed," McDonald said. "Losing is the worst thing, but we have a lot to look at and we have a lot to get better at. Get better this week and get ready for Notre Dame."

articles.standfirst: El Getafe suma sus ocho puntos en casa y su feudo vuelve a ser clave
articles.summary: El Getafe suma sus ocho puntos en casa y su feudo vuelve a ser clave
articles.body: El Getafe logró un triunfo clave en sus aspiraciones por el objetivo de la permanencia. El cuadro getafense sumó su segunda victoria del curso y demuestra el potencial de un equipo, el azulón, que necesitaba un resultado así después de cuatro fechas sin vencer. Los de José Bordalás lograron el primer triunfo contra el Real Racing de Santander en la segunda jornada y dos amargos empates frente a Deportivo de la Coruña y Celta tras haberse puesto frente a ambos equipos por delante. Ahora, contra los de Funes, los del sur de Madrid sumaron la segunda victoria y un bagaje final de ocho puntos. Todos ellos en un Coliseum que vuelve a sonreír y a ser un fortín, a celebrar goles cada partido y a ser la piedra angular del objetivo de la temporada, que es el de la permanencia y disfrutar en Conference League. De hecho, en Europa el Getafe también logró vencer en la ida de los playoffs para meterse en la Fase Liga del torneo continental, con el 3-1 que le endosó al Partizan que sirvió para clasificarse, pese a la también derrota en Belgrado en la vuelta. La cruz de este inicio de temporada son los duelos lejos del feudo getafense. El equipo aún no sabe lo que es sumar, con tres derrotas frente a Alavés, Osasuna y Real Betis, principal aspecto a corregir del equipo, que tendrá tres semanas de descanso durante el parón por selecciones.

articles.title: Rangers flip narrative as Derek McInnes makes mark
articles.summary: Consecutive Old Firm derby wins show Derek McInnes is starting to make his mark at Rangers after a mortifying start.
articles.body:
"I like putting my name to this team at the minute," Rangers manager Derek McInnes said after a second Old Firm derby win in a week.

That is hardly surprising, given the Rangers side that won 1-0 at Celtic Park in the league after last Sunday's 3-0 win at Ibrox in the League Cup is starting to look like a team built in McInnes' image.

A sluggish start to the campaign resulted in humiliating exits from the Europa League and Conference League and raised alarm bells among Rangers fans as they fell off the pace set by Celtic. The team looked completely lost.

Now, it is showing the hallmarks of its manager as they clinched a sixth straight victory and back-to-back derby triumphs to narrow the gap to Celtic to two points.

"Take it back a month when Derek McInnes was under real pressure," former Rangers midfielder Andy Halliday said on BBC Scotland's Sportsound.

"A big thing that was quite confusing to people is: 'it doesn't look like a Derek McInnes team'. They don't look organised off the ball, they don't look aggressive, they don't look athletic.

"How that narrative has completely changed over the last three, four weeks. That for me is a Derek McInnes team, what we watched today.

"Front foot, aggressive, making contact with people, when they win the ball back playing forward, running forward and putting Celtic under constant pressure for large parts of the game."

Naderi goal gives Rangers second derby win over Celtic in week

Watch: Scott Brown & Andy Halliday discuss Old Firm game on YouTube

All the Rangers reaction & have your say

McInnes conceded he is still "embarrassed" by the European exits against Jagiellonia Bialystok and Jablonec and said the criticism was hard to respond to earlier in the season.

But he has shown over 800 games as a manager that he can organise and motivate a team to be difficult to beat off the ball.

His Hearts side which went so close to winning the league last season conceded the fewest of any team in the Premiership. Rangers have conceded just once now in their last six games, having kept just one clean sheet in their first seven this season.

Dujon Sterling, playing in his best position of right-back, has formed a physically imposing unit with Emmanuel Fernandez and Olwethu Makhanya inside him.

That trio's defensive solidity allows James Penrice to maraud forward from left-back and help Rangers add numbers to their midfield.

Fernandez still has lapses in concentration. He was lucky not to be sent off at Celtic Park after an early booking for hauling down Camilo Duran was followed up by a dodgy challenge on Benjamin Nygren which went unpunished.

But once he settled, he repelled everything that came into Rangers' box, making 11 clearances. Makhanya next to him brings calm authority and was named man-of-the-match. Celtic were restricted to one shot on target at home.

In front of them, Dan Neil and Nico Raskin have stepped up in midfield. The pair made the most passes in Rangers' ranks, always showing for the ball and getting stuck in.

Rangers made 75 fewer passes than Celtic overall, but 50 more than their rivals in the opposition's half. While Celtic's passes were often between centre-backs, Neil and Raskin found each other and players in more advanced areas.

"My midfield were terrific again," McInnes said. "Celtic filled the midfield. We filled it with even more bodies, we just made sure we weren't going to get overrun in there.

"We look far more calm, far more settled in everything that we're doing. The players deserve so much credit for that."

When captain Lawrence Shankland pulled a hamstring against Motherwell having just started scoring regularly, it only raised concerns around Rangers.

Could Naderi and new £9m signing Kevin Kelsy fill the void? The former failed to wholly convince last season after a January switch from German third-tier side Hansa Rostock.

Now, he has four goals in 13 games, more than he managed in the second half of last season. His goal at Celtic Park was what Rangers will want more of.

Lurking to pounce when Kim Min-su's shot was parried out to him, he got his knee over the ball and finished smartly. But aside from his goal the 23-year-old German helped set the tone.

He was involved in an astonishing 34 duels, 18 of them in the air. He won 11 of them and worked so hard he was still panting for breath in his post-match interview.

To add to his physical presence, he had the most shots and touches in the Celtic box.

"His all round play was really, really good," former Rangers striker Kris Boyd said on Sky Sports. "Him and [Kevin] Kelsy didn't have much link up play but they were working together. If one went short, one went long.

"Naderi's running power was really key for Rangers. When he came in at first there was a rawness about him. But there is a lot to like.

"If Derek can get a hold of him and work with him and make him that complete striker, because he works his socks off and he can finish."

McInnes knows given the record investment in this Rangers squad, these sort of performances and results will be expected every week, especially without the burden of European football.

At an average age of 24, though, Rangers have one of the youngest groups in the league, and being shorn of their experienced captain Shankland only adds to that sense of rawness.

Former Rangers winger Peter Lovenkrands said on BBC Radio Scotland that the team will take "so much confidence" from beating their rivals twice in a row.

McInnes agrees this has to be the starting point, but becoming the first Rangers manager since Graeme Souness to win his first two derbies gives him a strong platform.

"There's a lot of growth in the team," the Rangers boss said. "And winning in places like this only helps. But there's plenty of league games to be won and we have to concentrate on that.

"It was hard to defend the criticism [at the start of the season]. We're on a strong run now, six wins in a row, which is the kind of consistency we're searching for.

"But at the start we didn't look ready, for whatever reason, we didn't look settled as a team, didn't carry an attacking threat.

"But we've knuckled down and worked hard, and hopefully that winning habit is something we can keep working towards."

articles.title: Man City 5-3 Sunderland: Enzo Maresca's side stay top of Premier League after chaotic eight-goal thriller
articles.summary: Report and free match highlights as Man City stay top of the Premier League after a chaotic but thrilling victory over Sunderland, including eight goals; Brian Brobbey scored a superb hat-trick but ended on the losing side
articles.body:
Enzo Maresca's side knew that any positive result would see them open up a gap on nearest rivals Arsenal after Mikel Arteta's side slumped to defeat at Brighton on Saturday. But Maresca surely did not plan to do it in the chaotic manner that transpired, with City trading blows with Sunderland as though it were a training match.

Enzo Fernandez's clever free-kick put City ahead inside nine minutes, but that was merely the beginning of the pandemonium. Rayan Cherki and Antoine Semenyo also found the net in a first half that produced five goals, with Sunderland's undefendable striker Brian Brobbey grabbing two.

Latest news and rumours: Man City | Sunderland

City's performance was littered with mistakes, particularly defensively, as Brobbey bullied Ruben Dias and completed a remarkable 33-minute hat-trick after Semenyo had netted his second of the afternoon to make it 4-2 in favour of the hosts.

Erling Haaland had the final say, breaking his Sunderland duck to complete the Premier League set, having now found the net all 25 opponents he has faced in the English top flight. Just another astonishing subplot from a ridiculous afternoon.

As a whole, the game could not have been further removed from the picture of control so often associated with Pep Guardiola's City. Out of possession, Maresca's blueprint left them alarmingly open, with Sunderland needing little invitation to exploit the gaps. Brobbey accumulated a personal expected goals value greater than every Premier League team this weekend, bar his own.

Sunderland might have left the Etihad empty handed but do so with plenty of credit after an attacking display that arguably outshone City's, registering nine shots on target. City's players sank to their knees at the final whistle, a clear indication of just how close they came to letting victory slip in the to and fro of such an intense battle.

"I prefer to win 1-0 than 5-3," Maresca concluded with a smile. "But I knew how difficult it would be."

9: GOAL! Fernandez opens scoring with a cheeky free-kick from a tight angle that beat Robin Roefs at his near post.

12: GOAL! Brobbey scores his first of the afternoon from Enzo Le Fee's sumptuous through ball.

29: GOAL! Cherki makes it 2-1 after Sunderland were caught overplaying around the back.

33: GOAL! Le Fee links with Thomas Meunier to hand Brobbey a tap in - which survives a VAR review for offside.

43: GOAL! Semenyo thunders a superb third for Man City after Marc Guehi does well to keep the ball alive in the box.

57: GOAL! Semenyo puts Man City 4-2 up with an emphatic finish into the far corner.

59: GOAL! Brobbey completes his hat-trick from Nilson Angulo's cross to pull the score back to 4-3.

70: CLEARANCE! Dias clears the ball miraculously off the line after Donnarumma failed to claim a cross.

82: GOAL! Haaland completes the scoring after being teed up by Josko Gvardiol.

Regis Le Bris: Belief remains high despite punishing loss

"We didn't compromise our identity. We're really proud to play our football and we went toe-to-toe with one of the best sides in Europe.

"We created many chances and every small mistake gets punished at that level. This is the reality of the Premier League and we're here to learn.

"The team is really resilient and the belief is high about our qualities, the way we can hurt the opponent. It's not a surprise, but we are frustrated because we came here with the belief it was possible to win."

On Brobbey's hat-trick: " It's positive because it's impossible to tell the story differently, but it's clear for us that he's a good striker, he's getting better with every game, and his mentality is superb. It was just a question of time."

articles.title: Leeds 0-0 Crystal Palace: Pierre Sage's side claim valuable point as Daniel Farke's team stay unbeaten in Premier League
articles.summary: Report and free match highlights as Crystal Palace battled to a 0-0 draw at in-form Leeds; Palace kept a clean sheet after conceding 11 goals in their opening four games, while Leeds remain unbeaten after five Premier League matches
articles.body:
The stalemate was enough to lift Sage's side one point clear of the relegation zone heading into the three-week international break.

Palace arrived having conceded 11 goals in their opening four Premier League games but, after a cagey first half, grew into the contest and were the more threatening side after the break. Tyrick Mitchell had the ball in the net only for it to be ruled out for offside.

Latest news and rumours: Leeds | Crystal Palace

Leeds, unbeaten coming into the game after an impressive 4-1 win over Newcastle, struggled to reproduce that attacking fluency. Dominic Calvert-Lewin, who had scored in each of his previous five Premier League home games, was largely starved of service, eventually being denied by Walter Benitez after the break.

Palace had chances to snatch it late on, with Adam Wharton continuing to influence proceedings and Eddie Nketiah and Ismaila Sarr combining for an opening that Tarik Muharemovic brilliantly recovered to stop. Leeds threw on attacking reinforcements and switched shape, but could not find the breakthrough.

For Palace, after conceding two or more goals in each of their previous 10 Premier League matches, they finally kept a clean sheet - and did so against a Leeds side that had scored 12 goals across their previous five home league games. The performance gives Sage a platform to build on after a difficult opening month.

10: SMART TACKLE! Muharemovic makes a crucial intervention to deny Jorgen Strand Larsen after Quinten Timber had slipped the Palace striker through on goal.

22: OVER! Ao Tanaka fires over from close range after Leeds' long throw caused problems in the Palace box.

31: PALACE PUSHING! Strand Larsen, Timber and Wharton all see efforts blocked as Palace threaten to break the deadlock.

53: OFFSIDE, NO GOAL! Mitchell fires Palace in front after Anan Khalaili's cross, but VAR confirms Khalaili was offside in the build-up.

57: WHAT A SAVE! Benitez produces an excellent reaction stop to deny Calvert-Lewin after James Justin's cross picked out the in-form striker.

71: PENALTY APPEAL! Daichi Kamada goes down under pressure from Ethan Ampadu, but the referee waves away Palace's claims.

83: BIG CHANCE! Wharton's clever ball releases Sarr into the area, but Justin recovers brilliantly to deny the Palace substitute.

88: PALACE OPPORTUNITY! Nketiah breaks clear after being played in by Wharton but chooses to square for Sarr, allowing Muharemovic to make a crucial recovery.

Palace showed exactly what they had been missing

Analysis by Sky Sports' William Bitibiri:

"Crystal Palace arrived at Elland Road with 11 goals conceded from their opening four Premier League games. They leave with a clean sheet and, on balance in the second half, will probably feel they could have taken all three points.

"This was a spirited, disciplined performance from Palace. They came out after the break with a completely different mindset and put Leeds under pressure.

"Leeds were strangely flat. Calvert-Lewin was starved of service for long periods and even when the chances did arrive, Palace goalkeeper Benitez was there to deny him.

"In the end, 0-0 feels like a reflection of two sides who cancelled each other out, but Palace can take far more encouragement from this performance than Leeds can.

"For Sage, though, this is the sort of defensive display he will hope can become the foundation of a turnaround."

Robinson: Neither side lost points - both gained one

"I thought Palace were excellent after the break.

"Both goalkeepers had to make excellent saves, but we were limited to few goalscoring chances. We witnessed two sides cancelling each other out.

"Neither side has lost points, but have gained one."

articles.title: Luke Littler's hopes of 2026 PDC major clean sweep over after defeat to Jonny Clayton at World Series of Darts Finals
articles.summary: Jonny Clayton ended Luke Littler's challenge in Amsterdam at World Series of Darts Finals and will now take on fellow Welshman Gerwyn Price in Sunday's second semi-final; Littler's hopes of calendar year clean sweep ended; Ross Smith faces Gian van Veen in other semi-final
articles.body:
The world No 1 had won the first six premier events of the season following his World Championship triumph at Alexandra Palace in January with the World Masters, UK Open, Premier League, World Cup of Darts and World Matchplay.

Littler was hoping to add the World Series of Darts Finals, World Grand Prix, European Championship, Grand Slam of Darts and Players Championship Finals trophies to complete a historic monopoly over the year - but ran into an inspired Clayton.

Clayton will take on fellow Welshman Gerwyn Price in Sunday's second semi-final, after England's Ross Smith meets home favourite Gian van Veen in the first semi-final, with the final to follow.

Littler can still sweep the ranking events - the World Series Finals, like the World Cup and Premier League, is non-ranked - if he wins the remaining four majors in Leicester, Dortmund, Wolverhampton and Minehead this autumn.

'The Nuke' has work to do to reach the Players Championship Finals, though, as he sits 125th on the Order of Merit in that series with six events of the regular season remaining and only the top 64 players advance to the finale in Somerset from November 27-29.

The teenager - currently £16,750 adrift of the final qualification spot - had hinted he may not try to reach the Players Championship Finals should his hopes of a major sweep end in the Netherlands.

The next Players Championship events are in Den Bosch on Tuesday and Wednesday before two more at the same venue on October 28 and 29 and then a final two in Leicester on November 4 and 5.

Clayton: Not the Littler we know but I took my chances

Jonny Clayton to ITV4 after victory over Luke Littler:

"To be honest, I just thought: 'Relax, go out and try your best.'

"What a player he [Littler] is. He wasn't full flow today, but you have to take your chances.

"Luke missed a lot of darts at doubles, and that's the name of the game. You have to take your chances. I did that and it's brilliant.

"The last dart in a double hurts, and it puts pressure on a player.

"All respect to Luke, he's fantastic but he gave me chances upon chances, and that's not the Littler we all know. But Jonny Clayton can play darts as well."

Van Barneveld: Everyone is fallible - Littler felt the pressure!

"It's the pressure. Everyone talks about: 'Can he do the whole year and win all the big majors.' It gives big pressure. He wants to perform.

"He's the best player at the moment, but everyone is fallible. Everyone wants your scalp, and Jonny Clayton did it perfectly.

"In all honestly, Littler missed some crucial shots.

Littler latest big name to exit in Amsterdam

Victory at the World Series of Darts Finals would have been Littler's second in three years, having beaten Michael Smith to triumph in 2024 before losing to Michael van Gerwen in the final 12 months ago.

Littler had suffered scares earlier this week, rallying from 3-1 down to defeat Danny Noppert 6-4 in round one and then surviving a last-leg shoot-out versus Nathan Aspinall to win 10-9 in the last 16.

World No 2 Luke Humphries was eliminated by Dirk van Duijvenbode in round two on Saturday, while defending champion Van Gerwen fell in the opening round on Thursday, losing to Daryl Gurney.

Van Gerwen's World Series Finals victory last season is the only major he has won since 2023 and he has failed to reach an individual quarter-final in this year's majors.

The 37-year-old did make it to the final of the World Cup of Darts for Netherlands alongside doubles partner Van Veen, where the Dutch duo were beaten by England's Littler and Humphries.

That World Cup victory for Littler in Frankfurt in June means the European Championship is the only major title absent from his CV - something he will hope to rectify in Dortmund later this year.
